a55.speaker: US State Department
a55.speech: Said it was implementing the designation of Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi movement as a "foreign terrorist organization." A State Department spokesperson said Tuesday's action implements the January decision to re-designate the Houthis.

a55.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a55.speech: "The Houthis' activities threaten the security of American civilians and personnel in the Middle East, the safety of our closest regional partners, and the stability of global maritime trade." ; "The United States will not tolerate any country engaging with terrorist organizations like the Houthis in the name of practicing legitimate international business."

a55.speaker: Stephane Dujarric, UN Spokesperson
a55.speech: "A designation like this must be coupled with appropriate safeguards and reassurances, both humanitarian assistance and the ability of civilians to commercially access central goods and services." ; "For humanitarian goods a lot of it comes in through the private sector. If this is not possible, it will have a devastating humanitarian impact." ; Pointed out that some 19 million Yemenis require life-saving assistance.

a55.speaker: Jakob Larsen, Chief Safety and Security Officer with the BIMCO shipping association
a55.speech: Warned that the designation "has the potential to deteriorate the security situation." ; Said those traffic patterns "are largely unchanged" and that given the Gaza ceasefire's uncertain future and the potential for U.S. or Israeli strikes on the Houthis, "the security threat is increasing."

a55.speaker: Houthi movement leader (unnamed)
a55.speech: Said the militants would monitor implementation of an Israel-Hamas ceasefire and resume strikes on commercial vessels or Israel if the deal was breached.

a55.speaker: Houthis
a55.speech: Said their attacks on shipping were in solidarity with Palestinians over Israel's war against Hamas in Gaza.

a179.speaker: Daily Maverick (report cited)
a179.speech: Reports today that the legacy of last year's scorching El Nino event is now receding in southern Africa and several countries in the region have just been removed from the UN's Hunger Hotspot list as harvests have significantly improved from the previous season's drought.

a179.speaker: UN World Food Programme (WFP) and Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO), semi-annual Hunger Hotspots report
a179.speech: "Ethiopia, Kenya, Lebanon, Lesotho, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, Niger, Zambia and Zimbabwe have been removed from the Hunger Hotspots list" ; "In east and southern Africa, as well as in Niger, better climatic conditions for harvests and fewer weather extremes have eased food security pressures. However, the FAO and WFP warn that these gains remain fragile and could reverse quickly if shocks re-emerge."

a179.speaker: Hunger Hotspots report (WFP/FAO)
a179.speech: "The latest Hunger Hotspots report shows that Sudan, Palestine, South Sudan, Haiti and Mali are hotspots of highest concern, with communities already facing famine, at risk of famine or confronted with catastrophic levels of acute food insecurity due to intensifying or persisting conflict, economic shocks and natural hazards," the report said ; "The devastating crises are being exacerbated by growing access constraints and critical funding shortfalls," it pointedly noted.

a179.speaker: Barchart (data compiled)
a179.speech: According to data compiled by Barchart, the futures price for South African white maize has fallen from record territory of more than R5,400 a tonne in January to about R4,700 a tonne, a drop of 13%.

a179.speaker: Global weather forecasters
a179.speech: Most global forecasters currently see the El Nino-Southern Oscillation remaining neutral until at least November, when there is a roughly 50/50 chance seen of La Nina making a return.

a309.speaker: Refugees International (NGO, statement)
a309.speech: Warned on Wednesday that "aid is desperately needed in Mozambique" for the thousands of displaced people caused by a new wave of "gruesome" extremist violence in Cabo Delgado, affecting more than 20,000 people in recent days; "The attacks have been especially gruesome and unpredictable in the country's northern province of Cabo Delgado, marked by abductions, killings, and sexual assaults. Many of those displaced have already been forced to flee multiple times, part of a total of 1.3 million people who have been displaced due to conflict, cyclones, and drought since 2017" ; pointed out that 'Humanitarian actors are sounding the alarm that massive cuts in foreign assistance are worsening the humanitarian and security situation,' recalling that support from the United States alone has fallen from $821 million in aid to Mozambique in 2024 to $243 million in 2025, with HIV/AIDS programmes, emergency response and health "among the sectors that have lost funding" ; "These cuts are part of a wider picture of aid groups shrinking or ceasing operations altogether due to funding shortages. Some have remained on shoestring budgets, even as aid workers are targeted, and some have had to suspend work in certain areas due to deteriorating security conditions" ; advocated the re-establishment of US and European Union support: "The United States and the European Union need to restore aid to the region. In particular, the European Union's Humanitarian Aid for Mozambique should scale up its efforts for immediate life-saving assistance. Regional actors must also provide diplomatic and security support to secure the region and ensure humanitarian access" ; said that "without an immediate surge in humanitarian assistance and global attention, Mozambique's civilians will face growing devastation as the fighters targeting them are emboldened to expand their reach."

a309.speaker: Mark Wood, Refugees International
a309.speech: Warns that "The recent increase in insurgent attacks across villages and towns in Cabo Delgado in northern Mozambique has led to a rapidly growing humanitarian and displacement crisis even as cuts in international aid have hobbled the humanitarian response"; says the "latest surge in attacks by armed groups, including a group that links itself to the Islamic State, has been mostly aimed at civilians and has led to at least 20,000 people being newly displaced, half of them children, as of September 24, 2025".

a309.speaker: Refugees International 2024 report
a309.speech: Had already highlighted "risks women and girls face in displacement in northern Mozambique, including early and forced marriage, sexual exploitation, and survival sex"; emphasises that "The conflict also continues to fuel family separation and an increase in unaccompanied minors".

a309.speaker: Official figures
a309.speech: By the end of July, attacks by these groups displaced more than 57,000 people in Chiure district, south of Cabo Delgado.

a309.speaker: Africa Centre for Strategic Studies (ACSS) study
a309.speech: In 2024 alone, at least 349 people died in attacks in northern Mozambique, most of them claimed by the extremist group Islamic State, an increase of 36% on the previous year.

a309.speaker: Refugees International (@RefugeesIntl) social media post
a309.speech: "Insurgent attacks across Cabo Delgado in northern #Mozambique have led to a rapidly growing humanitarian and displacement crisis. Armed groups must cease attacks on civilians and donor countries must surge aid for protection and life-saving services."

a383.speaker: Olegário Banze, Deputy Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development of Mozambique
a383.speech: In order to safeguard the venture, which cost more than 124 million meticais, speaks of more efficient marketing, and says the financing system needs to be improved.

a522.speaker: Surfshark (report by the Netherlands-based internet monitor)
a522.speech: According to a report by Surfshark, there were nine internet restrictions in eight African countries in the first half of 2023 - double the number of restrictions the same time last year.

a522.speaker: Surfshark (statement)
a522.speech: Said the restrictions were related to political turmoil and protests ; "All of Africa's new restrictions were imposed amid protests or other political turmoil, highlighting the critical role the internet plays during periods of civil unrest," the organisation said in a statement.

a522.speaker: Gabriele Racaityte-Krasauske, spokesperson for Surfshark
a522.speech: Said there would likely be more internet restrictions across Africa because of elections and military involvement in civilian affairs.

a522.speaker: Gabriele Racaityte-Krasauske, spokesperson for Surfshark
a522.speech: Said the shutdowns left people with no means to communicate with the outside world: "When the internet is restricted, people are left with limited opportunities to spread information to the rest of the world, organising protests, medical aid for people in need, and contacting friends and loved ones. It's important to spread the word on this because the people affected often have limited opportunity to do so themselves."

a562.speaker: Prof. Maxwell Darko Asante, new Director of CSIR-Crops Research Institute (CSIR-CRI), Ghana
a562.speech: In his acceptance for the new role as Director, noted that the appointment comes at a critical time when Ghana's agricultural sector is grappling with challenges such as climate change, soil degradation and post-harvest losses; according to him, under his leadership CSIR-CRI is expected to play a pivotal role in developing innovative solutions to these issues; indicated that his expertise positions him well to lead the institute in addressing these challenges in collaboration with the Ghanaian government, the private sector, stakeholders in Ghana as well as international partners.

a576.speaker: Venancio Mondlane, Mozambique opposition leader
a576.speech: Announced on Sunday that he would return ahead of the new president’s inauguration, saying in a Facebook live address he would arrive at Maputo’s Mavalane airport on Thursday; called for demonstrations against the results of the 9 October election, which he says were rigged in favour of the ruling Frelimo party ; “If they are killing my brothers, they are murdering my brothers, then I will be there. If it’s for me, if it’s because of Venancio, then Venancio will be today at Mavalane International Airport.” ; insists the election was stolen from him and that another count said he was the winner.

a576.speaker: Venancio Mondlane, Mozambique opposition leader
a576.speech: Appeared to shrug off criminal and civil charges laid against him: “You can do whatever you want,” he said, apparently addressing the authorities. He added: “If you want to murder, murder. If you want to arrest, arrest too. I will be there.” ; has previously claimed there had been attempts to assassinate him.

a576.speaker: Local rights group (tally)
a576.speech: The violence has left around 300 people dead, according to a tally by a local rights group, with authorities also reporting looting and vandalism.

a576.speaker: Final official results of the poll
a576.speech: Said Mondlane took 24% of the presidential vote compared to 65% for the Frelimo candidate, Daniel Chapo.

a576.speaker: International observer missions
a576.speech: Several international observer missions have also said there were irregularities.

a576.speaker: Filipe Nyusi, President of Mozambique
a576.speech: Has called for dialogue among the parties to resolve the dispute.

a576.speaker: Daniel Chapo, Frelimo president-elect
a576.speech: On 27 December last year called for “non-violence” and “unity”, saying several police officers had died during the clashes.

a576.speaker: Samia Hassan, President of Tanzania (chairing the SADC security troika)
a576.speech: Said the regional grouping SADC was concerned that the situation “may jeopardise peace and security for the country concerned and the region as a whole” ; “For the last couple of weeks, we have witnessed the spread of violent protests that have caused massive harm to human life, affected economic activities and disrupted cross-border trade.”

a576.speaker: Chansa Kapaya, UNHCR regional director for southern Africa
a576.speech: “Refugees and civilians are facing immense risks, losing their livelihoods and relying on humanitarian assistance” ; “While we are grateful for the generosity of Malawi and Eswatini, immediate support is crucial to tackle the worsening crisis and prevent further suffering.”

a707.speaker: General Mamadi Doumbouya, President of the Transition of Guinea (address to the nation)
a707.speech: Highlighted Guinea's "remarkable" diplomatic achievements, testifying to his vision of a strong and united Africa and his commitment to a more equitable world: "This year, Guinea has asserted itself as a determined actor on the international stage, where our diplomacy has been considerably strengthened further, and our partnerships have been consolidated. Our voice resonates louder than ever, thanks to our initiatives for a more integrated and united African and international cooperation. In a few years, Guinea has reached a record number of diplomatic representations, exceeding forty countries. This testifies to the confidence that nations place in our commitment to the sustainable and responsible socio-economic development of our country. These indicators show that we are resolutely on the right path. We have actively contributed to the construction of a more united, stronger, more resilient Africa, while promoting peace on a global scale. Together, we have shown that Guinea is no longer a mere observer, but rather an engaged leader in the management of African and world affairs. We will continue to further strengthen our relations with brother countries of the continent and of the whole world for the well-being of the population and to consolidate a community of shared destiny." ; "Strong in this leadership, in a pan-African spirit, the Republic of Guinea will continue to give its unfailing support to Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger for the success of their respective transitions. Once again, division serves only the one who divides. We must continue to focus on finding African solutions for the well-being of our populations."

a808.speaker: Onjezani Kenani, writer and social commentator (statement shared on social media)
a808.speech: Has raised serious concerns about President Lazarus Chakwera’s State House expenditure, questioning the moral and economic justification behind the administration’s lavish spending; highlighted a stark contrast between the budgets allocated to the State House during different presidencies, noting that during Peter Mutharika’s tenure the highest budget for the State House was $10 million ; “Akutani nazo ndalama za aMalawi abale?” Kenani asked in his native Chichewa, which translates to “What is he doing with Malawians’ money, brothers and sisters?”

a818.speaker: Jens Laerke, spokesman for the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
a818.speech: Said that of those 198 trucks, 90 have already been collected by various humanitarian organisations and associations so that their contents, which include nutritional products, medicines and flour, can be distributed. “Significant challenges persist in the loading and distribution of cargo due to insecurity, the risk of looting, and the routes provided by the Israeli forces, which are inadequate for the movement of cargo,” Laerke stressed.

a818.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a818.speech: Warned last week that half a million inhabitants of Gaza were on the brink of famine because of Israel’s “deliberate blockade”, and that 57 children had already died of malnutrition since the beginning of March.

a818.speaker: Stéphane Dujarric, spokesman for the UN Secretary-General (statement)
a818.speech: “On Wednesday, 21 May, the United Nations collected around 90 trucks at the Kerem Shalom crossing which were sent to Gaza,” declared the spokesman for the UN Secretary-General in a statement, without specifying the exact destinations.

a818.speaker: Local sources in Gaza (anonymous)
a818.speech: Said that the trucks carrying humanitarian aid that entered Gaza through the Kerem Shalom crossing in recent days have already begun distributing flour to different bakeries in the Gaza Strip; indicated that the bakeries of Khan Yunis and of the three areas of central Gaza already have flour to start making bread and feed a population subjected to a total blockade of food, fuel or medicine imposed by Israel since 2 March.

a818.speaker: Cogat, Israeli military body in charge of coordinating the entry of aid into Gaza
a818.speech: Confirmed that the trucks had begun distributing their loads to the destination centres.

a818.speaker: Israeli Prime Minister
a818.speech: Said on Wednesday that he was ready to accept a “temporary ceasefire” in the Gaza Strip that would allow the release of the last 20 hostages, and that he subsequently intends to take control of the entire Palestinian enclave.

a834.speaker: Government of Niger
a834.speech: Terminated the headquarters agreement of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) yesterday, ordering it to close its offices and leave the country, without disclosing the official reasons for the break.

a834.speaker: Nigerien authorities
a834.speech: In November 2024, expressed their dissatisfaction with the management of European Union humanitarian aid, accusing the ICRC and other NGOs of having designated the beneficiaries of the aid unilaterally, without prior consultation with them.

a844.speaker: Matthew R. Simmons, energy analyst
a844.speech: Estimates the true number of Saudi Arabia's proven crude oil reserves to be far less than the claimed 266.58 billion barrels.

a844.speaker: General Accounting Office report (1978)
a844.speech: The last non-Saudi report only mentioned 110 billion barrels of crude oil reserves.

a844.speaker: Sultan Abdul-Rahman Al-Dakhel, Ambassador of Saudi Arabia to Ghana
a844.speech: Said Saudi Arabia is Ghana's oldest bilateral partner in the Gulf Region and the relations between the two countries had paved the way for the expansion of its bilateral relations to the rest of the countries in the region.

a844.speaker: Collins Adumako-Mensah, Deputy Minister of Energy of Ghana
a844.speech: Commended the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia for its contribution to the socio-economic development of the country, especially in the areas of energy, educational development, humanitarian assistance, agriculture and infrastructure ; Said Ghana's relations with the kingdom dated back to the 1960s and the fruitful cooperation had culminated in the signing of a number of agreements between the two countries, including the recent agreements on military cooperation, an agreement between the Ghana Export Promotion Authority and the Saudi Export Agency, with the aim of promoting non-oil exports and business opportunities between the two countries.

a844.speaker: Collins Adumako-Mensah, Deputy Minister of Energy of Ghana
a844.speech: Encouraged Saudi investors to take advantage of the conducive business climate in Ghana and the opportunities presented by the African Continental Free Trade Area to do business in the country; he enumerated a number of projects the Saudi government had undertaken in Ghana, including the recent rehabilitation and expansion of the Bolgatanga Regional Hospital to improve health care in Ghana ; Said Ghana was resolved to cooperate with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to promote global peace and security, and assured the international community of a peaceful and fair general election on December 7.

a859.speaker: William Ruto, President of Kenya
a859.speech: Said in remarks at the London Stock Exchange on Wednesday that Kenya is planning to privatise some state assets via initial public offerings in order to bring in more private sector investment, that the government plans to start with listing the Kenya Pipeline Company via an IPO on the Nairobi Securities Exchange this year, and that well-functioning domestic capital markets could reduce reliance on external debt.

a859.speaker: William Ruto, President of Kenya
a859.speech: Said at the Africa Debate event that following shocks such as U.S. President Donald Trump's elimination of USAID this year, Kenya is working to rely on its own resources, and private investments, rather than "resources that we do not have any control over." ; He cited plans to partner with the private sector to provide hospital equipment on a fee-per-use basis and said Kenya had raised $1.3 billion by securitising assets such as roads to raise funding: "We are now going to be listing some of those bonds in the securities exchange so other investors can have a bite of the cherry."

a1193.speaker: Lesley Mkandawire, economist
a1193.speech: Said these realities leave limited fiscal space for bold economic recovery measures. "The economy is doing badly. Prices of goods are rising rapidly, and it is everyone's expectation that the next budget should bring recovery."

a1193.speaker: World Bank's Malawi Economic Monitor (MEM) report
a1193.speech: Highlighted the worrying trend, noting that while overall spending was 14.2 percent below target, crucial sectors such as public sector wages continued to spiral out of control. "With liquidity constraints in the domestic securities market, the government had to scale down domestically financed projects to accommodate wage bill increases."

a1193.speaker: Bertha Bangala Chikadza, President of the Economics Association of Malawi
a1193.speech: Emphasizes that investment in productive sectors is the only way to spur long-term economic recovery. "The budget should be in line with MIP-1. We need production, so productive sectors need serious investments."

a1193.speaker: Thomas Munthali, Director General of the National Planning Commission
a1193.speech: Argues that sustainable revenue generation - not reliance on borrowing - is the key to economic stability. "If we are relying on borrowing and resources from external partners, it is not going to work. It's high time we developed internal capacity for revenue generation and mobilization for sustainable development."

a1193.speaker: Simplex Chithyola Banda, Minister of Finance of Malawi
a1193.speech: Has hinted at efforts to cut the deficit while increasing production-related spending.

a1293.speaker: John Mutorwa, Deputy Prime Minister of Namibia
a1293.speech: expressed deep gratitude for the assistance, highlighting the importance of international solidarity in times of crisis. "This generous donation from your respective countries, your excellencies, is a true reflection of international solidarity, our shared humanity, and the noble responsibility to help one another in times of crisis," Mutorwa said. ; "These contributions have significantly empowered our efforts as a country to assist those in dire need. We extend our sincere and profound gratitude to all our international partners for their unwavering support."

a1293.speaker: John Mutorwa, Deputy Prime Minister of Namibia
a1293.speech: said that despite the rains across the country over the past few weeks, the drought remains a problem. "These figures include different age groups, from the elderly to parents and children, who experience the harsh reality of hunger and loss of livelihoods. As a caring government, it is our responsibility to attend to the plight of affected citizens," Mutorwa said.

a1293.speaker: John Mutorwa, Deputy Prime Minister of Namibia
a1293.speech: says the scale of the crisis has outstripped available financial resources, with a funding shortfall of approximately N$600 million needed to sustain relief efforts until June this year.

a1293.speaker: 2024/25 livelihood vulnerability assessment and analysis conducted by the Office of the Prime Minister
a1293.speech: revealed that approximately 1.2 million Namibians – 41% of the population – are currently food insecure.

a1293.speaker: Nangolo Mbumba, former President of Namibia
a1293.speech: declared a state of emergency in May 2024 in response to the drought crisis.

a1313.speaker: European Commission
a1313.speech: Unveiled on Tuesday a plan to “rearm Europe” intended to mobilise nearly 800 billion euros for its defence, and also to provide “immediate” aid to Ukraine after the freezing of American aid. The Commission wants to facilitate national defence spending by member states, to make some 150 billion euros of loans available to the 27 EU countries for arms purchases or investments, to use cohesion funds for defence projects, to facilitate recourse to the European Investment Bank, and to mobilise the private sector for defence financing in Europe.

a1313.speaker: Ursula von der Leyen, President of the European Commission
a1313.speech: In a letter addressed to the leaders of the 27: “Europe faces a clear and immediate danger of a magnitude that none of us has known in our adult lives.” ; “The future of a free and sovereign Ukraine, of a secure and prosperous Europe, is at stake.” ; Added that the project would also make it possible to help Ukraine “immediately”, after US President Donald Trump's decision to freeze military aid to Kyiv ; Confirmed her intention to encourage states to spend more on their defence without regard for the budget rules obliging them to limit their public deficit to 3% of GDP: “This will allow member states to increase their defence spending significantly without triggering the excessive deficit procedure,” citing an amount of 650 billion euros over four years ; Assured that with this equipment “member states will be able to massively strengthen their aid to Ukraine. So, immediate military aid to Ukraine.”

a1313.speaker: Camille Grand, defence expert at the ECFR and former NATO official
a1313.speech: Interviewed by AFP, said: “It can make it possible to finance or accelerate certain purchases,” but added, “the results will be visible in a few weeks or a few months rather than ‘immediately', but it matters because the effects of the American restrictions will also be felt in a few months.”

a1313.speaker: Nadia Calvino, President of the European Investment Bank (EIB)
a1313.speech: Called for the range of eligible investments to be broadened, according to a letter on Tuesday seen by AFP (the bank is not currently authorised to finance projects directly linked to the defence sector).

a1313.speaker: A European official (anonymous)
a1313.speech: Specified that this would include strictly military projects.

a1313.speaker: Kaja Kallas, EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs
a1313.speech: Has put forward a proposal to strengthen military aid to Ukraine, which the 27 leaders will also discuss; several amounts, up to 30 billion euros, have been floated.

a1313.speaker: A diplomat in Brussels (anonymous)
a1313.speech: Said a decision among the 27 on the Kallas proposal is unlikely on Thursday.

a1628.speaker: Joseph Mwanamvekha, Malawi Minister of Finance, Economic Planning & Development (on devaluation and the Washington mission)
a1628.speech: Has assured that there will be no devaluation of the Kwacha, having secured substantial international support in Washington D.C.; said the mission to Washington D.C. - sanctioned by President Arthur Peter Mutharika - focused on stabilising the economy and addressing challenges related to the 4 Fs: food, foreign exchange, fuel and fertilizer supply.

a1628.speaker: Joseph Mwanamvekha, Malawi Minister of Finance (on international support secured)
a1628.speech: Revealed that the World Bank has provided US$45 million for emergency food assistance targeting four million Malawians, while the African Development Bank has also pledged additional support, with the IMF expected to visit Malawi in the first week of November to assist efforts to stabilise the economy; also announced that the Chinese government has forgiven Malawi's US$20 million debt and granted an additional US$3 million to support the country, while on its part the government is cutting expenditures, reforming policies, and restructuring debt to ensure fiscal sustainability.

a1628.speaker: Joseph Mwanamvekha, Malawi Minister of Finance (on priorities and the Mpatamanga project in talks with the IFC)
a1628.speech: Outlined five immediate priorities - food, fertiliser, foreign exchange, fuel, and pharmaceuticals - aimed at addressing the needs of the general population, and expressed the Government's strong desire to see the Mpatamanga Hydropower Project commence without delay, noting that its timely implementation would help address Malawi's persistent power shortages and support broader industrial and economic development; he welcomed the IFC initiatives, noting that the Government would greatly appreciate the planned private sector diagnostic study as its findings will provide valuable insights to inform policy direction and strengthen private sector participation in national development.

a1628.speaker: Joseph Mwanamvekha, Malawi Minister of Finance (on reform commitment, to the IMF)
a1628.speech: Assured the IMF delegation of the Mutharika administration's strong political will, reaffirming that the President has already started fiscal measures to strengthen economic stability, including minimising unnecessary external and internal travel, promoting virtual meetings and advancing ongoing engagements with bilateral and multilateral partners to restructure debt.

a1628.speaker: Joseph Mwanamvekha, Malawi Minister of Finance (on Saudi cooperation)
a1628.speech: Expressed appreciation for the strong and longstanding partnership between Malawi and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and reaffirmed Malawi's commitment to collaborate closely with Saudi counterparts in advancing projects that directly address the country's development needs; further emphasised that Malawi is prioritising economic reforms aimed at promoting stability, creating jobs, and improving the livelihoods of Malawians.

a1628.speaker: Malawi Government official Facebook page
a1628.speech: Reports that a media briefing on Food Crisis Support was held at the Ministry of Finance upon the Minister's return.

a1628.speaker: International Finance Corporation (IFC)
a1628.speech: Reaffirmed its continued support for the realisation of the Mpatamanga Hydropower Project in Neno District.

a1628.speaker: Ethiopis Tafara, IFC vice-president for Africa
a1628.speech: Is reported to have reiterated IFC's strong partnership with Malawi and invited the Minister to outline the Government's key priorities; assured the Minister that IFC, as the lead arranger of financing for the Mpatamanga Project, is on track with the due processes required to reach financial close, and outlined several IFC-supported initiatives in Malawi, including advisory support for the Shire Valley Transformation Programme and the development of student accommodation in public universities, adding that IFC plans to undertake a private sector diagnostic study focusing on agriculture, tourism, and mining.

a1628.speaker: World Bank Group
a1628.speech: Has reaffirmed its strong partnership with the new government administration and committed to provide support for food assistance during the current lean season.

a1628.speaker: Ndiame Diop, World Bank Group regional vice-president for Eastern and Southern Africa
a1628.speech: Pledged the Bank's continued support towards advancing Malawi's development and economic reform agenda.

a1628.speaker: Abebe Selassie, Director of the IMF's African Department
a1628.speech: Held a meeting focused on Malawi's macroeconomic priorities, including debt sustainability, inflation management, economic growth, and fiscal deficit reduction, and sought to understand Malawi's reform priorities and the country's commitment to sound macroeconomic management.

a1628.speaker: Eric Meyer, US Department of the Treasury deputy assistant secretary for Africa and the Middle East
a1628.speech: Acknowledged the macroeconomic challenges Malawi is facing and reaffirmed continued US bilateral support aimed at cushioning the impact of current economic pressures; took cognizance of the adverse effects of post-USAID funding cuts on key sectors, particularly health, and expressed optimism about the resuscitation of US development programmes, assuring that discussions are underway with the Global Health team to explore renewed support for Malawi's health sector, focusing on HIV/Aids, tuberculosis, and related areas; he further advised the Government of Malawi to continue intensive discussions with the IMF on debt sustainability and management as a pathway to unlocking further investment and development opportunities.

a1628.speaker: Mohammed Aljadaan, Saudi Minister of Finance & head of the Saudi Mission to the IMF and World Bank
a1628.speech: Reaffirmed his country's commitment to deepen collaboration with Malawi in key sectors such as energy, infrastructure development, road construction, and humanitarian support.

a1628.speaker: Saudi delegation
a1628.speech: Confirmed that the Saudi Government had granted a no-objection for the Roads Authority to sign a consultancy services contract for the Makanjira road project; as financiers, expressed optimism that construction will soon progress and reaffirmed their continued support for its successful completion; and extended a cordial invitation to Malawi's Ministry of Tourism to participate in the upcoming 26th UN Tourism General Assembly, scheduled to take place in Riyadh from November 7-11, 2025.

a1807.speaker: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
a1807.speech: Issued a new alert on Monday 16 September about the risks of avian influenza reappearing in certain countries, warning that the H7N9 and H5N1 avian influenza viruses are once again prowling around poultry; said it had disbursed about one billion CFA francs in emergency funds, to which is added USAID's contribution, estimated at about 2.5 billion; said it is continuing its fundraising appeal in order to support the global response to H7N9, and urged countries to take measures to clean up the livestock production sector so as to keep this threat away from their producers.

a1807.speaker: Juan Lubroth, FAO chief veterinary officer
a1807.speech: Sounded the alarm during a joint meeting with the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), the World Health Organization (WHO) and the World Organisation for Animal Health (OIE); according to him, the means of responding to the announced viruses do indeed exist, thanks to the decade of work accomplished on the H5N1 virus, and the recent response to H7N9 is tangible proof that these means exist. "Vigilance must not be relaxed, since avian influenza viruses are still circulating in poultry," he indicated.

a1808.speaker: Government of Burundi
a1808.speech: Has expressed deep concern over the escalating security crisis in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), which has triggered a large influx of refugees into Burundian territory since the beginning of the year; according to government estimates, between 20,000 and 35,000 people have crossed the Rusizi River into Burundi since February 1, with an additional 5,000 arriving through the Gatumba border post, the majority being asylum seekers in need of international protection, with the influx increasing significantly since February 14.

a1808.speaker: Ministry of Internal Affairs and Public Security of Burundi (statement)
a1808.speech: "The persistent violence in eastern DRC has led to an unprecedented flow of refugees into our country. The Government of Burundi recognizes the dire circumstances faced by these asylum seekers and is committed to upholding its humanitarian obligations."

a1808.speaker: Ministry of Internal Affairs and Public Security of Burundi (statement)
a1808.speech: "The government is mobilizing all necessary resources to provide immediate assistance to those in need. We are working closely with ONPRA, UNHCR, and other partners to ensure the safety and well-being of all asylum seekers."

a1808.speaker: Government of Burundi
a1808.speech: Said new refugees will be relocated to the Musenyi site in Rutana Province to ensure their safety and provide adequate living conditions, and that additional sites will be allocated to UNHCR and its partners to accommodate the continuous arrival of refugees.

a1808.speaker: Ministry of Internal Affairs and Public Security of Burundi (statement)
a1808.speech: Called upon the national and international community for solidarity and support in responding to this humanitarian crisis: "We urge all stakeholders to join hands in assisting these vulnerable populations. This is a humanitarian issue that requires collective action."

a1808.speaker: Ministry of Internal Affairs and Public Security of Burundi (statement)
a1808.speech: Urged Burundians to maintain their tradition of hospitality towards Congolese refugees while remaining vigilant against misinformation spread through social media platforms, which they say could disrupt public order: "We call on Burundians to welcome our Congolese brothers and sisters with warmth and solidarity. At the same time, we caution against rumors and misinformation that seek to create unnecessary panic and instability."

a2260.speaker: Fadumo Omar, 40-year-old displaced mother from Qoryoley district living at Al-Hidaya camp
a2260.speech: "We used to receive food and support from USAID. Now we have nothing. No food, no water, not even toilets." ; "We came here to survive, but things are getting worse." ; "We don't have much left. But we still have hope."

a2260.speaker: Residents of Al-Hidaya camp
a2260.speech: Said they have received no aid in recent months amid the U.S. funding freeze.

a2260.speaker: Somali government and aid agencies
a2260.speech: According to the Somali government and aid agencies, the abrupt suspension of funding threatens to derail humanitarian operations nationwide.

a2260.speaker: Abdullahi Dahir Ahmed, program manager at the Somali Women Development Center
a2260.speech: Said that critical services have been disrupted since the U.S. aid was halted: "We are doing everything possible to find new partners. But it's not easy. Local donors do not have the capacity and many international donors are also overwhelmed by other crises around the world." ; Observed that even European donors are now considering cuts of up to 50 percent -- further shrinking the pool of support available to Somalia's most vulnerable citizens ; "The loss of U.S. aid has already affected our ability to serve people in need. If these trends continue, the situation will become much more dire, especially for displaced families who rely on this aid to survive."

a2260.speaker: Fadumo Abdulkadir, 42, displaced woman from Lower Shabelle
a2260.speech: Said the reduction in aid from both the U.S. and the United Nations has had a devastating impact: "We used to get food and small cash payments. Pregnant women and malnourished children also got nutritional supplements. Now, there's nothing. This has affected us a lot." ; "We are just trying to survive... We need aid agencies to resume their support before it's too late."

a2260.speaker: Somali government
a2260.speech: Has urged continued engagement and pledged greater transparency in aid delivery.

a2260.speaker: Humanitarian workers
a2260.speech: Say they can do only so much with dwindling resources.

a2272.speaker: Former Defense Minister Yoav Gallant, former IDF Chief of Staff Herzi ("Zither") Halevi, and former Shin Bet Director Ronen Bar
a2272.speech: Cautioned Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu repeatedly: without a clear plan for the "day after" in Gaza, any military victory would be rendered meaningless ; Again and again, across media channels and news outlets, the message was clear—Israel must create a new political reality in Gaza.

a2272.speaker: Bezalel Smotrich and Itamar Ben Gvir, Netanyahu's far-right coalition partners
a2272.speech: Had already threatened to topple the government if he pursued such a path (a ceasefire leading to a state commission of inquiry and likely new elections).

a2272.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli Prime Minister, and Israel Katz, Minister of Defense
a2272.speech: Continue to order the IDF forward, recycling empty slogans about "total victory" (no longer fashionable) or "opening the gates of hell".

a2272.speaker: Hamas
a2272.speech: Has not collapsed; it refuses to surrender.

a2281.speaker: Hands-Off Basotho Movement (Basotho migrants working and studying in South Africa)
a2281.speech: Want Local Government, Chieftainship, Home Affairs and Police Minister Lebona Lephema fired for his "incompetence and dishonesty". They are frustrated with Mr Lephema's failure to issue them with passports on time or at all. They also accuse him of failing to effectively engage with South African authorities regarding work permits, study permits, and new Lesotho Exemption Permit (LEP) applications. They say they will petition Prime Minister Sam Matekane next week demanding that he fires Minister Lephema for "incompetency and dishonesty".

a2281.speaker: Semenyane Linale, President of the Hands-Off Basotho Movement
a2281.speech: Told the Lesotho Times yesterday that they had already applied for a permit from the Maseru City Council (MCC) to march and deliver the petition to the Prime Minister. Mr Linale said Mr Lephema was incompetent and had grossly failed Basotho. His ministry's perennial failure to issue critical documents timeously and inability to effectively engage with South African authorities over the status of Basotho in that country had caused them significant inconveniences and jeopardized their living circumstances. Mr Linale accused Minister Lephema of "endless lies" and making "empty promises". ; "We want Mr Lephema removed as minister due to his incompetence and his administration's constant lies." ; "Basotho are struggling to get passports and other crucial identity documents, yet Mr Lephema has been telling us that passports are available and that he is engaging with South Africa to facilitate easier movement. All of this has turned out to be lies."

a2281.speaker: Semenyane Linale, President of the Hands-Off Basotho Movement
a2281.speech: Said the situation of Basotho in South Africa remained dire with many being routinely arrested and abused by their employers with no help from their government. ; Chastised Mr Lephema for "falsely" claiming that the governments of Lesotho and South Africa had reached an agreement to grant 90-day visas to Lesotho nationals studying and working in the neighbouring country. He said South African immigration officials consistently denied the existence of such an agreement. ; "We are also concerned about the minister's false promises regarding the 90-day visa. That has turned out to be another lie, and we are tired of listening to his empty rhetoric."

a2281.speaker: Senate's Government Assurances Committee (GAC)
a2281.speech: On September 3, 2024, the Senate's Government Assurances Committee (GAC) publicly chastised him for misleading them about the department's ability to seamlessly issue passports to Basotho. The GAC strongly criticized Mr Lephema for providing inaccurate information that his ministry was on top of a crisis that had left many Basotho unable to access passports and national ID documents.

a2281.speaker: Lerato Nkhetse, Director of the Migrant Workers Association (MWA-Ls)
a2281.speech: Echoed Mr Linale's sentiments, saying that Basotho working and studying in South Africa without proper documentation were facing severe problems. However, Mr Nkhetse did not believe that Mr Lephema intentionally lied about negotiations with South Africa. Rather, he suggested Mr Lephema lacked an effective feedback mechanism and often miscommunicated the details of these negotiations. ; "Mr Lephema often raises the hopes of Basotho by prematurely announcing negotiations, only to fail to provide any follow-up feedback. He is often overwhelmed by political excitement and reveals information too early. He needs to be more careful with how he communicates messages to the public."

a2281.speaker: Lerato Nkhetse, Director of the Migrant Workers Association (MWA-Ls)
a2281.speech: Highlighted a key challenge with Mr Lephema's ministry, that migration issues were often negotiated in isolation, without input from migrants themselves or other directly affected stakeholders. "Migratory matters are complex and require inclusive consultations so policymakers are well-informed about what is being negotiated," he noted. He said Lesotho was grappling with high unemployment, leading many Basotho to seek work in South Africa, and it thus made sense that the government take a firm interest in dealing with migration matters affecting its citizens.

a2281.speaker: Lebona Lephema, Minister of Local Government, Chieftainship, Home Affairs and Police (non-response)
a2281.speech: Attempts to reach Mr Lephema for comment were unsuccessful, as his phone went unanswered.

a2848.speaker: Elia Kaiyamo, Namibia’s (outgoing) ambassador to China
a2848.speech: Described his posting as “an honour and a privilege, marked by significant achievements across diplomacy, economics and culture. I do not claim individual credit but rather see my role as building upon the excellent foundation laid by my predecessor, the late Comrade Peter Mweshihange, and all ambassadors who came before me.”

a2848.speaker: Elia Kaiyamo, Namibia’s ambassador to China
a2848.speech: “I devoted considerable effort to creating opportunities for Namibian students to study in China and to expanding cultural exchanges. These human connections are the bedrock of a lasting bilateral relationship.” ; “The most lasting achievement has been fostering understanding between Namibians and Chinese through education, culture and business. Student exchanges, the Confucius Institute, and the Chinese Bridge competition have all built meaningful, lasting connections.”

a2848.speaker: Elia Kaiyamo, Namibia’s ambassador to China
a2848.speech: Highlighted the practical outcomes of the partnership: “China has become Namibia’s largest trading partner, and significant investments in mining, energy and agriculture have created thousands of jobs while contributing substantially to our tax base.”

a2848.speaker: Elia Kaiyamo, Namibia’s ambassador to China
a2848.speech: Acknowledged challenges but emphasised careful diplomacy: “Even when difficult discussions arose, they were handled in the spirit of Sam Nujoma and Mao Zedong, with respect and understanding.”

a2848.speaker: Elia Kaiyamo, Namibia’s ambassador to China
a2848.speech: Stressed: “Industrialisation and value addition are key – we must move beyond exporting raw materials. China’s role in technology transfer will be crucial.” ; “We must keep the legacy of Sam Nujoma and Mao alive. It will serve as a strong foundation for the years ahead.”

a2848.speaker: Zhao Weiping, China’s ambassador to Namibia
a2848.speech: Noted that Chinese investments in the Husab and Rössing uranium mines account for 6 to 7% of Namibia’s GDP and provide nearly 6 000 jobs ; added that China is Namibia’s second-largest trading partner and a major source of foreign investment, with bilateral trade reaching US$2.08 billion in 2024.

a2848.speaker: Zhao Weiping, China’s ambassador to Namibia
a2848.speech: Noted that China provides over 200 training opportunities and 50 scholarships annually, alongside development assistance in education, health, agriculture and infrastructure: “These initiatives reflect China’s commitment to friendship, mutual benefit and South-South cooperation.”

a2848.speaker: Zhao Weiping, China’s ambassador to Namibia
a2848.speech: Reaffirmed that Chinese cooperation comes without political conditions, rooted in equality and mutual respect ; highlighted ongoing projects in renewable energy, artificial intelligence, space technology and green hydrogen, alongside the satellite ground station in Windhoek, demonstrating China’s support for Namibia’s modernisation goals.

a2848.speaker: Zhao Weiping, China’s ambassador to Namibia
a2848.speech: “China has always been, and will continue to be, a reliable and close partner of Namibia. Our cooperation brings tangible benefits to our peoples and strengthens the solidarity of the Global South.”

a2920.speaker: Wilhelmina Diop, Group CEO of HelloSolar
a2920.speech: Confirmed that HelloSolar is currently running a pilot project, in partnership with BelCash, Shell Foundation, DFID, USAID and Power Africa, to test its PAYGO model with end-to-end distribution, installation and after sales services.

a2920.speaker: Mountaga Vince Diop, founder and CEO of BelCash
a2920.speech: “We’re very happy to participate in enabling the first PAYGO and international remittance payment” with HelloSolar in Ethiopia and contribute to giving access to affordable energy solutions to the Ethiopian off-grid population.”

a2920.speaker: Osman Ibrahim, Country Director of HelloSolar Ethiopia
a2920.speech: “In addition to making our solar home systems affordable through PAYGO, we also make sure to provide best-in-class services with our end-to-end distribution, installation and after sales services.”

a2920.speaker: Bart Minsaer, General Manager of HelloSolar
a2920.speech: “After the pilot project, HelloSolar will adapt and roll out its model nationwide and be at the prime position to achieve the Ethiopian government’s target of providing 3.5 million solar home systems by 2025.”

a2920.speaker: Michael Tesfaye Hiruy, HelloSolar Chief Strategy Officer
a2920.speech: “Our mission goes beyond providing affordable access to energy” ... “moving forward, we will forge the necessary partnerships to provide access to connectivity through affordable smartphones and digital services such as healthcare, education, market access and employment”.

a3034.speaker: UNRWA, the main UN aid agency in Gaza
a3034.speech: Said an Israeli strike a day earlier hit one of its warehouses in the southern city of Rafah, killing an employee ; said in a statement at least one staff member was killed and 22 wounded “when Israeli forces hit a food distribution centre in the eastern part of Rafah.”

a3034.speaker: Israel
a3034.speech: Said a Hamas militant was killed in the rocket strike on Rafah and identified him as Muhammad Abu Hasna.

a3034.speaker: Yoav Gallant, Israeli Defence Minister
a3034.speech: Vowed again that Israeli forces “will reach every location” in their mission to destroy the Islamist group.

a3034.speaker: Gaza health ministry
a3034.speech: Said Israeli forces have killed at least 31,272 people in Gaza, most of them civilians ; said 79 people were killed in Gaza between Wednesday evening and Thursday morning, among them seven killed when Israeli troops opened fire on a group of people at Kuwait Junction, an aid distribution point just south of Gaza City ; said four people were killed in the strike on the UNRWA facility.

a3034.speaker: Gaza health ministry
a3034.speech: Said the dire food shortages in Gaza have killed 27 people through malnutrition and dehydration, most of them children.

a3034.speaker: 25 organisations, including Amnesty International and Oxfam (joint statement)
a3034.speech: Said in a statement on Wednesday that airdrops and efforts to open a maritime corridor were “no alternative” to land deliveries because they could only provide a fraction of the aid needed.

a3034.speaker: Marine Traffic, specialist website
a3034.speech: Reported that the Open Arms vessel was moving slowly south off the coast of Israel.

a3034.speaker: Eid Ayub, Gaza City resident
a3034.speech: “They send aid, but when this aid arrives, there's no entity to distribute it,” adding that aid by sea and air “is not enough.”

a3034.speaker: Constantinos Kombos, Cypriot Foreign Minister
a3034.speech: Said on Wednesday a second aid ship “with bigger capacity” was being prepared in Larnaca.

a3034.speaker: Joint statement of Cyprus, US Secretary of State Antony Blinken and senior ministers and officials from Britain, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, the European Union and the United Nations
a3034.speech: Called on Israel to open the port of Ashdod, north of Gaza, for aid deliveries; the statement said senior officials will gather in Cyprus on Monday for “in-depth” briefings on the maritime corridor.

a3034.speaker: Israeli military
a3034.speech: Said the UN's World Food Programme had sent an initial six aid trucks along an alternative land route from southern Israel through a gate in the security fence into northern Gaza on Tuesday.

a3034.speaker: AFP count based on official figures
a3034.speech: The 7 October Hamas attack resulted in about 1,160 deaths in Israel, mostly civilians.

a3034.speaker: Israel
a3034.speech: Believes about 130 captives remain in Gaza but that 32 of them are dead.

a3034.speaker: Philippe Lazzarini, UNRWA chief
a3034.speech: Said the attack “comes as food supplies are running out, hunger is widespread and, in some areas, turning into famine.”

a3034.speaker: Stephane Dujarric, spokesperson for the UN secretary-general
a3034.speech: Told reporters that “the Israeli army received the coordinates... of this facility.”

a3034.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli Prime Minister
a3034.speech: Reiterated on Wednesday the warning by Israeli officials that ground troops would be sent into Rafah.

a3034.speaker: Agnes Callamard, Amnesty International secretary general
a3034.speech: Said air drops and sea shipments of aid “are a sign of powerlessness and weakness on the part of the international community.”

a3034.speaker: Fahd al-Ghoul, resident of Jabalia Camp
a3034.speech: “We have been fasting against our will for two months or more.” ; “Now with Ramadan, nothing changes in our reality.”

a3055.speaker: Paulus Hango, President of the Trade Union Congress of Namibia (TUCNA)
a3055.speech: Said trade unions and workers in Namibia face many challenges and difficulties ; says trade union leaders need to firmly commit themselves as a united front and help to ensure that workers earn decent wages and stop exploitation of the employees ; stated that employers make massive profits at the expense of the workers ; stressed that in the same way a conducive environment for investors is created, the same must be done for employees' working environments and better wages.

a3055.speaker: Paulus Hango, President of the Trade Union Congress of Namibia (TUCNA)
a3055.speech: "The minimum wage commission has already given the report to the Minister of Labour, and the Commission has recommended that at least N$18 per hour is an appropriate minimum wage for Namibian workers; however, the Minister of Labour, with full power invested in him by the Labour Act to implement the minimum wage, has chosen to remain silent and not implement the minimum wage. For trade unions, silence means refusal, and refusal means, the rejection of workers and support for capitalists who chose to exploit the workers." ; said there is a need for a national campaign to ensure that the minimum wage is fully implemented ; "There will be no more excuses. Just imagine some security guards earning N$8 per hour for the past seven years and working continuously without any rest, and all twelve hours that they work continuously are calculated as normal hours. This is not acceptable. We must come up with a resolution and strategy to free trade unions and workers from exploitation. Trade unions are subject to a variety of restrictions that hinder their activities and effectiveness."

a3207.speaker: Olavo Correia, Cabo Verde’s Finance Minister (Deputy Prime Minister)
a3207.speech: In an interview with Lusa on Thursday in Washington, said that Cabo Verde has not yet been officially notified about the closure of that US government agency, but stressed that, according to “the data he has, there is a very strong probability of that happening” ; it is a decision that “harms Africa and harms Cabo Verde. We cannot disguise this” ; “We will only take a formal position on this issue when the Government is notified. But of course, as Finance Minister, I look at this with some concern, because it is a project for which we had great expectations in terms of amounts and in terms of sectors. Hearing the information that it may be closed is something that worries us” ; “As political managers, what we have to do is this: we cannot adopt an attitude of lamentation. So, if it is a fact, we have to accept it as such when we are informed, and look for other partnerships. That is our role. But of course I would not like to receive that communication” ; said he was prepared for that possibility and stressed that the Cabo Verdean Government “is already looking for alternatives to this eventual closure of the MCC package” ; “If that programme ends up being closed, there is nothing to lament. It is a fact, we take note of it and we have to look for alternatives to compensate for that financing ‘gap’ and find solutions so that investments continue in Cabo Verde. This is our obligation: to look to the future and look for solutions. No crying; what matters is optimism and work to make things happen.”

a3207.speaker: Several media outlets
a3207.speech: Reported on Thursday that the MCC, which supports development projects mainly in African countries, including Portuguese-speaking ones, will suffer “significant reductions” in the number of staff and programmes.

a3207.speaker: Internal memorandum cited by France-Presse (AFP)
a3207.speech: States that the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), led by billionaire Elon Musk, will impose “significant reductions” in the number of staff and programmes of this agency.

a3207.speaker: Politico (US news site)
a3207.speech: Adds that the agency is expected to lay off its 320 employees and end grants to some 40 developing countries where it has projects.

a3207.speaker: Data from the Ministry of Finance (Cabo Verde)
a3207.speech: According to data from the Ministry of Finance, Cabo Verde benefited from its first MCC compact in July 2005, when the Government and the US agency signed a five-year agreement worth 110 million dollars (97 million euros) to help increase the country’s economic growth and reduce poverty through investments in infrastructure, watershed management and support for agriculture, and private sector development.

a3207.speaker: Olavo Correia, Cabo Verde’s Finance Minister (Deputy Prime Minister)
a3207.speech: On Donald Trump’s tariff plan: although he acknowledged that the direct impact on the country’s economy will not be significant, he admitted that he fears the indirect effects, namely on the financial relations that Cabo Verde has with Europe, but also on the “remittances of Cabo Verdean immigrants who are in various geographies and who will be affected by these tariff measures,” while not ruling out an economic recession ; “Of course the United States is not a major trading partner of Cabo Verde, but we are not outside these consequences. We may have smaller direct consequences, but the indirect ones are there and can be very visible in a short space of time.”

a3221.speaker: Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA)
a3221.speech: Said it is projecting a massive revenue leap to over N1.27 trillion in 2025, representing a 40 percent increase from the N894.86 billion it realized in 2024; the Authority says this ambitious target is anchored on sweeping modernization efforts, the full activation of the Dangote Refinery's marine operations, and the deployment of cutting-edge technology to enhance port efficiency.

a3221.speaker: Abubakar Dantsoho, Managing Director of the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA)
a3221.speech: Disclosed this in his presentation during a budget defence session with the House of Representatives Committee on Ports and Harbours: "Our 2025 budget proposal is more than figures, it reflects our aspirations for a more efficient, globally competitive port system," adding that over 70% of the proposed expenditure will go into capital projects ; revealed that only N417.86 billion, less than half of the approved N850.92 billion expenditure, had been spent as of the time of reporting ; "This shows our unwavering commitment to national revenue generation, even when our own operational liquidity is affected" ; said the projected revenue increase is premised on several key assumptions and developments, including the full operation of the Dangote Refinery expected to draw in over 600 vessels annually through its Single Point Mooring (SPM) system, the commissioning of upgraded terminals at WACT and OMT, the implementation of automation tools such as the National Single Window, Port Community System (PCS) and Vessel Traffic Management System (VTMS), and increased cargo volumes stemming from global disruptions including the Russia-Ukraine conflict ; said the 2025 revenue is expected to come from Ship Dues, N544.06 billion; Cargo Dues, N413.06 billion; Concession Fees, N249.69 billion; and Administrative Revenue, N73.07 billion.

a3221.speaker: Abubakar Dantsoho, Managing Director of the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA)
a3221.speech: Said the capital investment will target the revitalization of critical infrastructure, including the Calabar, Warri, and Burutu ports and channels, and enhance towage services, channel depth, and compliance with international security conventions ; "Investments in infrastructure and technology are non-negotiable if we are to stay competitive regionally and globally" ; cited increasing competition from neighboring ports and aging assets across Nigeria's coastal corridors ; "We can say that with timely access to internally generated revenue and capital funds NPA would deliver the kind of impact Nigeria expects."

a3221.speaker: Hon. Nnolim Nnaji, Chairman of the House Committee on Ports and Harbours
a3221.speech: Urged the NPA to ramp up performance, improve port infrastructure, and play a greater role in addressing Nigeria's revenue and unemployment challenges; said the ports remain a critical pillar of Nigeria's economy and urged the agency to meet rising expectations despite operational challenges: "No country can thrive economically without high-performing ports. They are the economic heartbeat of every nation, determining how buoyant a country is through the flow of imports and exports" ; stressed that the NPA's performance has implications beyond maritime activity, noting that increased port output can significantly boost job creation across several sectors: "The Nigerian Ports Authority is not just a revenue-generating agency, it is a national asset in terms of employment and economic impact. We expect to see detailed strategies on how to improve revenue generation and expand employment opportunities through your 2025 budget" ; pointed to growing interest in the development of new ports across the country but cautioned against neglecting existing port infrastructure: "As we welcome investment in new ports, we must not abandon the old ones. Maintaining and upgrading our existing ports, both in the Eastern Corridor and the Western axis, is essential to long-term sustainability."

a3221.speaker: House of Representatives Committee on Ports and Harbours
a3221.speech: The committee praised NPA for its performance; the Committee called for a clear outline from the NPA on how its 2025 financial plan will address pressing national concerns and reaffirm Nigeria's competitiveness in regional and global maritime trade.

a3230.speaker: Pempho Trinity Chikoleka Maliro ('Complex'), Malawian hip-hop artist
a3230.speech: "I quit when I lost my job, and I could not afford studio or promotion fees. Women struggle to get through the creative or arts sector in Malawi. Doors are always blocked; in some cases, women are taken advantage of," she said in an interview ; "I still write, but I had to lie low as I had no finances, and it was difficult for me to penetrate the industry. There are just so many challenges that women in the arts face."

a3230.speaker: Anganile Nthakomwa, deputy director of arts (Censorship), Department of Arts, Ministry of Local Government, Unity and Culture
a3230.speech: "This study is more than just numbers; it reflects the lived realities of women creatives in Malawi. Our role as government is to ensure that these findings inform policies and programmes that truly dismantle the barriers women face in the cultural and creative industries" ; emphasized: "We want to see gender desks become action-oriented spaces. They must not exist on paper only, but actively provide platforms for women to report challenges, access mentorship, and influence decision-making within associations" ; concluded: "If we are to unlock the full potential of Malawi's creative economy, women must be at the centre of it. Their voices, talents, and leadership are essential to building an inclusive sector that not only preserves culture but also drives economic transformation."

a3230.speaker: Report: Gender Mapping and Institutional Assessment of Cultural and Creative Associations in Malawi (Unesco-funded study)
a3230.speech: Highlights disparities across the 12 arts associations, including music, literature, photography, visual arts, theatre, fashion, folk music and dance; notes that despite boasting a female president, the Film Association of Malawi (Fama) has far more male than female members; notes that limited financial returns drive women out of the sector: "An individual cast in a movie, regardless of the role, is paid only K15 000 for the entire production period, equivalent to approximately $7. Such minimal compensation makes the film industry an unattractive option, prompting women to invest their time in other business ventures that offer greater financial stability and return" ; recommends the establishment of gender desks within associations, which would oversee the implementation of constitutional provisions aimed at increasing women's participation and ensure the development and enforcement of comprehensive gender and anti-harassment policies; states that the Fashion Association of Malawi plans to secure funding to expand its outreach to women designers, tailors, and fashion entrepreneurs, particularly in underserved regions.

a3230.speaker: Felistus Tibalenge Ngwira ('Nya-Uyu'), comedian
a3230.speech: Adds that societal expectations further stifle women's creativity and ambition: "Women often have to work harder to prove themselves in a male-dominated industry. They often face biases and barriers that limit access to resources, funding, and networking opportunities. This imbalance affects the diversity and richness of our creative landscape. Men get to have more than women. I have seen incidents where men are given sponsorship deals easily than women, and at times the ideas of women are far better than men's, but we see their doors being shut" ; supports the idea of gender desks: "To promote greater gender equality and inclusivity in the creative sector, we need institutional changes such as providing more targeted funding and resources for women-led projects, establishing mentorship programs that pair women with industry leaders, and implementing policies that ensure equal opportunities and representation. Additionally, creating safe spaces for women to share their work and ideas without fear of judgment or marginalisation is crucial. By implementing these changes, we can foster a more inclusive and equitable creative sector that allows women to thrive and reach their full potential."

a3230.speaker: Lilly Alfonso, fashion designer
a3230.speech: Believes gender strongly influences opportunities in the creative sector: "Women often have to work twice as hard to prove themselves in environments where leadership and recognition are still male-dominated. Cultural expectations also mean women juggle more responsibilities outside of their careers, which can limit their opportunities. Yet, I believe women's perspectives bring richness, diversity, and a different kind of strength to the creative industry" ; notes that arts associations and institutional support remain inconsistent, and the creative economy policy framework is still developing: "There has been some progress as organisations like the British Council are supporting programs such as the Creative DNA Malawi initiative, which I lead, in partnership with the 100 Year Plan initiative. But there must be dedicated funding streams for women creatives, alongside mentorship and training programs. Secondly, the government and private sector should recognise the creative economy as a serious contributor to GDP, and design policies that make it easier for women to access markets locally and internationally. Inclusivity should not just be a word - it should be reflected in budgets, policies, and representation."

a3230.speaker: Lilly Alfonso, fashion designer
a3230.speech: Agrees that the creative industries are more than just cultural expressions - they are also about job creation, youth empowerment, and export potential: "This is why I came up with the 100-Year Plan. It is a call for the next generation of Malawian creatives to think ahead of time, to plan ahead of time, and to create things that will outlast us for the next 100 years. By building products and brands that endure, we attract massive attention and trust from the international community. It is about time to turn the world's eyes towards Malawi, and to do so, we must commit ourselves to excellence, long-term thinking, and innovation."

a3247.speaker: Ussene Isse, Mozambican Minister of Health
a3247.speech: Warned that the "significant and abrupt" reduction in international funding is having "alarming" effects on the health sector, worsening difficulties in areas such as logistics, supply of medicines and human resources: "Amid the growing challenges in health, there is also the significant and abrupt reduction in international funding in the health sector, the impact of which is already proving alarming for the country," he said during the biannual meeting to define and implement health sector policies and strategies in Maputo ; "Indeed, we have a moral duty to prevent anything that may happen and that is inevitable for our populations and I take this opportunity, once again, to highlight the issue of having a single strategic operational approach" ; explained the impacts of these cuts in international funding on logistics, the supply chain of medicines, transport and also on human resources, calling for funding for the health sector.

a3247.speaker: Ussene Isse, Mozambican Minister of Health
a3247.speech: Stressed the need to discuss new forms of funding: "I want to take this opportunity to launch a great challenge to all of us, to have a national dialogue on the financing of the health sector. One plan, one financing and a single monitoring plan. This is what will guide us in this decision that we will have to make together."

a3247.speaker: Ussene Isse, Mozambican Minister of Health
a3247.speech: Said professionals have a "clear mission" not to allow Mozambicans to suffer from "preventable diseases" due to a lack of "good care", medicines or other hospital consumables, and set out priorities: "It is in this context that we have defined the following priorities: strengthening the resilience of the supply chain of medicines, surgical medical supplies, reagents and others, integrated planning and financing starting at district level and strengthening public finance management."

a3247.speaker: Ussene Isse, Mozambican Minister of Health
a3247.speech: Defended the need for reforming the Ministry of Health in order to "focus on the priorities" of Mozambique: "We have to bring something that will benefit patients first and foremost and anything that is done or suggested that will not benefit patients, we will not allow that to happen in the Ministry of Health, because resources are scarce and we have to do a lot with the little that we have."

a3247.speaker: Severin R von Xylander, World Health Organization (WHO) Representative in Mozambique
a3247.speech: Supported the minister's call for funding for the health sector and warned of the impacts in that area.

a3451.speaker: International Monetary Fund
a3451.speech: Praised Somalia's reform momentum but warned that the country's economic outlook has weakened, with growth projected to slow to 3 percent in 2025, down from 4 percent the previous year, weighed by foreign aid cuts, climate shocks and global uncertainty; stressed the need to press ahead with customs modernization, the new income tax law and civil service pay and pension reforms to ensure fiscal sustainability.

a3451.speaker: Bihi Iman Egeh, Somalia's Finance Minister
a3451.speech: Opened the fourth review meeting of the country's Extended Credit Facility program with the IMF in Nairobi on Sunday, speaking as senior officials from the Federal Government of Somalia looked on, with discussions focused on fiscal reforms and economic progress tied to IMF support.

a3636.speaker: Dr Nguéto Tiraïna Yambaye, director general of the African Guarantee and Economic Cooperation Fund (Fagace)
a3636.speech: "The African continent is potentially rich but chronically underfinanced because conventional banking institutions are reluctant to grant productive credit."

a3636.speaker: Jules Ngankam, director general of the African Guarantee Fund (AGF) Group
a3636.speech: "Despite the internationally recognised importance of SMEs, small African businesses face difficulties in accessing financing for their growth and innovation needs."

a3636.speaker: World Bank (World Development Indicators 2024)
a3636.speech: On average, bank deposits represent less than 20% of GDP in several West African countries, compared with more than 40% in Asia or Latin America.

a3636.speaker: Dr Nguéto Tiraïna Yambaye, director general of Fagace
a3636.speech: "Our interventions are 80% directed at SMEs," explains Dr Yambaye, recalling that Fagace sets up guarantee lines and supports project promoters in drawing up their business plans. "Our role is to push banks to contribute to development, particularly in the sectors they often avoid, such as agriculture and livestock," he insists.

a3636.speaker: Jules Ngankam, director general of the African Guarantee Fund (AGF) Group
a3636.speech: "AGF is the missing link that enables banks to effectively carry out their SME financing strategies."

a3636.speaker: Abdourahmane Diallo, director general of the African Solidarity Fund (FSA)
a3636.speech: "Determined, committed and responsible, the Fund is dedicated to building together with its partners a better and sustainable future."

a3636.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a3636.speech: SMEs make up more than 80% of the African economic fabric.

a3636.speaker: World Bank (Global Findex 2025)
a3636.speech: Around 58% of adults in sub-Saharan Africa had a bank account or mobile money account in 2024, compared with 34% in 2014.

a3636.speaker: Experts and institutions
a3636.speech: Advocate strengthening regional cooperation in order to foster synergies among the different guarantee funds and maximise their impact, as well as increasing the capitalisation of the funds, investing in training and developing awareness-raising programmes.

a3644.speaker: Egyptian Presidency (statement)
a3644.speech: According to the statement, the two politicians stressed the need for “the circle of conflict not to expand” in order to “avoid falling into a comprehensive regional war” that would have serious repercussions on the security and capabilities of all the countries and peoples of the region.

a3644.speaker: Abdel Fattah El Sisi, President of Egypt
a3644.speech: Called for “the continuation and intensification of international efforts” aimed at a ceasefire in Gaza and Lebanon, an end to the violations and attacks in the West Bank, and the provision of urgent and sufficient humanitarian aid to put an end to the growing suffering of civilians.

a3644.speaker: Tel Aviv (Israeli government)
a3644.speech: Stated that it would respond to Iran's launch of dozens of ballistic missiles against Israel on 1 October.

a3644.speaker: General Hossein Salami, commander-in-chief of Iran's Revolutionary Guard
a3644.speech: Warned that Tehran will respond “painfully” if Israel attacks Iranian targets inside or outside the national territory.

a3808.speaker: The two parties (Djiboutian and Ethiopian delegations)
a3808.speech: held open, constructive and fraternal discussions and reached a consensus on most of the subjects addressed; they welcomed the work accomplished, which will make it possible to schedule the signing of the intergovernmental agreement in the very near future.

a3808.speaker: The two parties (Djiboutian and Ethiopian delegations)
a3808.speech: welcomed the clear political will at the summit level of the two States with a view to the completion of this joint project, and the excellence of the relations of friendship and cooperation between the two friendly and brotherly countries.

a3896.speaker: Committee of Concerned Scientists (letter)
a3896.speech: Has called on Sierra Leone President Julius Maada Bio to ensure the safety and academic freedom of Dr. Chernoh Alpha M. Bah; expressed alarm over Dr. Bah's inability to conduct essential archival and oral history research in Sierra Leone due to ongoing threats; urges President Bio to confirm Dr. Bah's right to return to Sierra Leone without fear of retribution or prosecution; demands an investigation into the threats against him and clarity on the government's actions to address them; emphasized that Dr. Bah should be free to meet with family, friends, and colleagues in the country ; highlighted Sierra Leone's obligation under its $480 million agreement with the United States Millennium Challenge Corporation to improve its human rights record and combat corruption, rather than targeting scholars like Dr. Bah ; stated it will closely monitor developments.

a3896.speaker: Alexander Greer, Professor at The City University of New York, signatory
a3896.speech: “We are deeply concerned that a scholar of Dr. Bah's caliber is unable to pursue his research due to threats” ; “Sierra Leone must protect academic freedom and address these serious allegations.”

a3896.speaker: Chernoh Alpha M. Bah, scholar and editor-in-chief of the Africanist Press
a3896.speech: Has not commented publicly on the matter.

a3896.speaker: Sierra Leone government
a3896.speech: Has yet to respond to the committee's requests.

a4042.speaker: Standard & Poor's (S&P), rating agency note
a4042.speech: Downgraded the rating of Mozambique's domestic debt issues to CCC-: "The government announced a plan to carry out liability management exercises on its local currency obligations. In general, we consider most debt swaps in the CCC category to be distressed and equivalent to a financial default," write the analysts; the note points out that "post-election economic disruptions are negatively influencing the government's budgetary and liquidity operations." S&P maintained its opinion on sovereign credit in Eurobonds but downgraded its outlook, signalling that a further downgrade in both cases is likely in the next 12 to 18 months.

a4042.speaker: Standard & Poor's (S&P), rating agency note
