a4042.speech: Foresees a widening of the budget deficit to 4.5% between 2025 and 2028, worsening the 4.2% forecast made in October last year, due to "falls in tax revenue, increased spending on security and weaker growth due to recent demonstrations"; warns that the expected debt swap with private banks, "which should involve an extension of terms and a review of interest rates", could lead to the attribution of a default "if the final terms of the exercise of debt liabilities resemble a distressed debt swap", adding that the analysis is made on a case-by-case basis and takes into account the political and macroeconomic context.

a4042.speaker: Standard & Poor's (S&P), rating agency note
a4042.speech: Says Mozambique is servicing its external debt without delay, worth 9% of GDP and costing US$81 million per year until 2028, rising to US$225 million per year between 2028 and 2031, while warning that "there remains a risk that the US$20 billion (EUR19.1 billion) Area 1 project could suffer further delays"; on external financing, analysts say "the baseline scenario assumes that Mozambique will continue to access financing under the three-year program with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), worth US$456 million (EUR436 million), but the budgetary slippage could postpone the last two disbursements, which cumulatively amount to US$126 million (EUR120 million), and jeopardize the potential signing of a new program after March 2025"; noting that Mozambique received US$664 million in 2023 from USAID, so "the current suspension of US financing worsens already difficult external financing conditions", and predicting a return to growth of 4.3%, above the 2.5% recorded last year, then 5.4% a year on average until 2028.

a4148.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a4148.speech: Is calling for US$ 1.5 billion for its 2025 Health Emergency Appeal (HEA), to support life-saving health interventions worldwide; the appeal outlines the critical priorities and resources needed to address 42 ongoing health emergencies, including 17 Grade 3 crises – the most severe emergencies requiring the highest level of response.

a4148.speaker: Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General
a4148.speech: “Conflicts, outbreaks, climate-related disasters and other health emergencies are no longer isolated or occasional – they are relentless, overlapping and intensifying. From controlling cholera outbreaks to providing mental health support in conflict zones, WHO’s work extends beyond the immediate care we provide. We empower communities to protect themselves, prioritize equity, and build a legacy of preparedness. This appeal is about enabling WHO to save lives, protect the right to health, and provide hope where there is none.”

a4148.speaker: WHO 2025 Health Emergency Appeal (document)
a4148.speech: Highlights four key challenges facing the world currently: climate change, conflict, displacement and disease outbreaks, which are responsible for fueling deeper, longer lasting health crises and putting the world’s most vulnerable at greater risk; and further details the priorities and financial needs for each of the Grade 3 emergencies that WHO is responding to.

a4196.speaker: Kano State Government (statement by Sanusi Bature DawakinTofa, Director General, Media and Publicity)
a4196.speech: Blamed opposition elements of misleading the general public, in a statement titled “KNSG Breaks Silence on Alleged Diversion of N6.5 billion”: “The digital media space in the last few days has been awash with a series of false narratives bordering on the accountability, trust, and financial worthiness of some key political aides of the Kano State Government.” ; “Central to the case of purported misappropriation, already under litigation at the High Court, is the Director General, Protocol Directorate, Kano State Government House, Alh. Abdullahi Rogo.” ; “Once again, for clarity, the Office of Protocol in any government or institution is purely administrative in function. Its mandate is to coordinate official engagements, state visits, receptions, ceremonial events, and logistics including handling honorarium, and other interventions as well as special assignments. It is not an independent spending office and does not undertake any financial transactions outside established rules and approvals. Every action undertaken by the Protocol Office is done within the framework of the law and with the express approval of the government the under a designated budget code” ; “The allegations being peddled are therefore nothing more than a work of fiction, carefully crafted by political opponents who have resorted to blackmail and propaganda in their desperation to remain relevant ahead of the 2027 elections.”

a4196.speaker: Kano State Government
a4196.speech: Said every cash outflow into Ministries, Departments, and Agencies is properly budgeted with clear codes well spelt out in the fiscal policy of the state, and that no individual in government MDAs handles public funds without proper designated purpose; said the administration of Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf will remain focused on governance and maintain its position on financial prudence, accountability, transparency, and zero tolerance for corruption, but will not sacrifice the integrity of its aides to deliberate acts of political blackmail being orchestrated by unpatriotic elements of society; said it is not in doubt of the credibility of the Director General, Directorate of Protocol, Hon. Abdullahi Ibrahim Rogo.

a4232.speaker: United Nations
a4232.speech: Has expressed grave concerns about the deteriorating humanitarian situation in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), where escalating violence is severely restricting access to vulnerable populations; is urgently calling for the creation of humanitarian corridors to allow the safe passage of displaced people seeking refuge and the delivery of vital aid.

a4232.speaker: UN News
a4232.speech: According to UN News, following intense clashes in Goma last week, a fragile calm has settled over the city, but tensions remain high; while sporadic gunfire has decreased within Goma itself, fighting continues in surrounding areas, especially in Sake, northwest of the city.

a4232.speaker: United Nations
a4232.speech: Has announced the appointment of Brazilian General Ulisses De Mesquita Gomes as the new MONUSCO force commander.

a4232.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a4232.speech: Cited the deaths of 13 South African soldiers in eastern DRC, attributing the escalation to the “M23 rebel group and the Rwandan Defense Forces (RDF).”

a4232.speaker: Paul Kagame, President of Rwanda
a4232.speech: In a series of posts on X (formerly Twitter), condemned what he called “deliberate distortions” and “lies” in the South African statements, insisting that the RDF is an army, not a militia.

a4232.speaker: General Ulisses De Mesquita Gomes, new MONUSCO force commander
a4232.speech: He has pledged to work with all mission components to “protect civilians” and contribute to building a better future for the Congolese people.

a4350.speaker: United Nations (UN)
a4350.speech: According to the UN, at least 19.5 million people will need aid this year in Yemen; the organisation expressed concern about malnourished children.

a4350.speaker: Joyce Msuya, UN Acting Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), speaking to the Security Council
a4350.speech: "The people of Yemen continue to face a grave humanitarian and civil protection crisis" ; "At least 19.5 million people in Yemen will need humanitarian assistance and protection this year, 1.3 million more than in 2024" ; added that "almost half" of the country's population, that is more than 17 million people, "cannot meet their basic food needs", expressing concern for the "most marginalised", such as women and girls or the 4.8 million displaced ; insisted that among those at greatest risk, "almost half of children under five suffer from severe stunting due to malnutrition" ; said the "terrible" level of the cholera outbreak had also increased the burden on an already "severely overstretched" health system.

a4540.speaker: Patrick Deboeck, Charge d'affaires of the Embassy of the Kingdom of Belgium in Mali
a4540.speech: Indicated that the humanitarian aid provided by his country aims to save lives, alleviate suffering and preserve the human dignity of populations affected by crises and disasters ; said that, according to him, agriculture and food security are key sectors of Belgian development cooperation, and that the World Food Programme is a privileged partner of his country, which recently signed a multi-year funding agreement.

a4540.speaker: Patrick Deboeck, Charge d'affaires of the Embassy of the Kingdom of Belgium in Mali
a4540.speech: Said that in Mali Belgium is supporting a project of 3 million euros, nearly 2 billion FCFA, contributing to better food and nutritional security: emergency food aid supporting vulnerable populations and Internally Displaced Persons during and after shocks through food vouchers or unconditional cash transfers, and nutritional aid for children under 5 suffering from severe malnutrition. “Through this project they will receive a daily ration in order to provide three nutritious meals a day” ; specified that this will help fight malnutrition among children and contribute to the development of the local economy by offering caregivers nutritious and diversified menus from local suppliers, and that an envelope of 500,000 euros within that amount is allocated to funding UNHAS, an agency whose work is indispensable to ensuring aid reaches the most vulnerable populations.

a4540.speaker: Ibrahima Diallo, Interim Country Director of the World Food Programme (WFP) in Mali
a4540.speech: Described a bleak picture of the food situation in Mali, which remains worrying in certain regions of the country; cited the March 2024 Cadre Harmonise figure of about 1,400,000 people in acute food insecurity, attributing the causes to the worsening of insecurity and to climate shocks that have displaced these populations. “The deterioration of the security situation in certain regions of the country has also strongly affected agriculture, fishing and livestock farming and has considerably reduced the livelihoods of many communities.”

a4540.speaker: Ibrahima Diallo, Interim Country Director of the World Food Programme (WFP) in Mali
a4540.speech: Indicated that thanks to the generous contribution of 3 million euros from the Embassy of the Kingdom of Belgium, WFP will be able to provide vital assistance to nearly 47,000 people, essentially internally displaced persons in the areas most affected by food insecurity, for four months. “This assistance will make it possible to meet the basic food needs of the communities affected by the aforementioned crises during and after the shocks” ; announced that nearly 6,000 caregivers (mainly mothers) will receive a food ration three times a day over a period of 3 months. “This crucial support to the parents of children suffering from malnutrition allows them to stay with and beside their children during treatment and gives them a chance to recover their health quickly.”

a4540.speaker: Cadre Harmonise (March 2024 analysis)
a4540.speech: Reports about 1,400,000 people in a situation of acute food insecurity in Mali.

a4540.speaker: Mohamed Ag Redwane Ali, Malian Minister Commissioner for Food Security
a4540.speech: Expressed the gratitude of the Malian people to the Embassy of the Kingdom of Belgium, indicating that this important support will allow WFP to expand its assistance programme in Mali; according to him 41,491 people will benefit from this emergency food aid over a period of 4 months, in the regions of Kayes, Koulikoro, Sikasso, Segou, Mopti, Menaka, Gao, Timbuktu and Kidal.

a4552.speaker: Joseph N. Boakai, President of Liberia (inaugural address)
a4552.speech: During his inaugural address, outlined his vision for the country, emphasizing unity, development, and the importance of addressing pressing issues such as corruption, economic recovery and social justice.

a4552.speaker: 2024 Global Hunger Index (GHI)
a4552.speech: Ranks Liberia 120th out of 127 countries for which sufficient data is available, with a GHI score of 31.9, classifying the level of hunger in the country as serious.

a4552.speaker: Social Cohesion and Reconciliation Index (SCORE)
a4552.speech: Findings indicate a significant decline in food security from 2018 to 2024, revealing that 80% of Liberians face the challenge of providing sufficient food for their families.

a4552.speaker: Center for Transparency and Accountability in Liberia (CENTAL)
a4552.speech: According to CENTAL, of the total 1,306 appointments made, 38 were embroiled in controversy, including 13 appointments that were altered or modified after their initial announcement and another 25 that became ineffective.

a4552.speaker: Center for Transparency and Accountability in Liberia (CENTAL)
a4552.speech: Publicly called for Abdullah Kamara's dismissal, urging that the GAC's audit findings warrant immediate action to restore credibility and integrity to the government.

a4552.speaker: General Auditing Commission (GAC) audit
a4552.speech: Revealed that during his time as CEO of TAMMA Corporation, Abdullah Kamara was involved in making unauthorized payments totaling L$262,844,500 and US$450,000, without adhering to established procurement protocols.

a4552.speaker: General Auditing Commission (GAC) report on the Central Bank of Liberia
a4552.speech: Uncovered serious compliance failures at the Central Bank of Liberia spanning from 2018 to 2023, prompting the suspension of Executive Governor J. Aloysius Tarlue.

a4552.speaker: United States government
a4552.speech: Is seeking Daniel Johnson, Secretary General for the Roberts Flight Information Region, for allegedly defrauding the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) out of approximately $1.9 million.

a4552.speaker: U.S. Department of State's Diplomatic Security Service (DSS)
a4552.speech: Classified Monrovia as a location with a CRITICAL threat level, indicating the potential for crime that could directly impact U.S. government officials and their interests.

a4552.speaker: Debt Management Office (third-quarter fiscal report)
a4552.speech: Latest figures show the national debt exceeded $2.5 billion by the conclusion of September 2024.

a4552.speaker: Joseph N. Boakai, then-candidate for President of Liberia (campaign pledge)
a4552.speech: Pledged that upon assuming office he would ensure that no vehicle would become stuck in the mud within his first 100 days, with his administration aiming to improve infrastructure nationwide and make all major corridors accessible and safe for travel.

a4552.speaker: Roland Giddings, Liberian Public Works Minister
a4552.speech: Publicly acknowledged breaching procurement protocols by awarding road maintenance contracts valued at $22.4 million without adhering to a competitive bidding process.

a4552.speaker: Government of Liberia
a4552.speech: Denied that any formal agreement was finalized with the Guma Group related to the exploration of the Wologizi mountain, under which 285 pieces of earth-moving equipment were reportedly provided.

a4552.speaker: Joseph N. Boakai, President of Liberia
a4552.speech: Publicly expressed unwavering confidence in Madam Miatta Fahnbulleh, the Chairperson of the inaugural committee ; issued a directive dated November 28, 2024 instructing all appointed officials to follow the Declaration of Assets requirements specified in the 2014 Code of Conduct ; dismissed Madam Carmerna Cephas Yeke from her position at NASSCORP citing “gross insubordination to the Office of the President”.

a4552.speaker: University of Liberia (UL) investigative committee report
a4552.speech: Concluded that Commerce Inspector D. Dorr Cooper had illegally obtained an undergraduate degree in Public Administration; according to the findings, Cooper allegedly paid $10,000 to members of the university staff to facilitate his impersonation of a deceased student, and the report recommended prosecution for his unethical actions.

a4552.speaker: Supreme Court of Liberia (ruling of April 24, 2024)
a4552.speech: Stated that Boakai's appointments of individuals to tenured positions in various government institutions directly violated established laws.

a4552.speaker: Fofana, Presidential Press Secretary of Liberia
a4552.speech: Addressed the media to clarify the president's use of chartered flights, emphasizing that there are circumstances where flying on chartered flights becomes necessary for the president. “Sometimes, taking chartered flights is not just a preference but a necessity. When the president is traveling to attend a significant meeting that requires his presence and is located within a relatively short distance, it is crucial that he can arrive efficiently and effectively.”

a4552.speaker: Senator Darius Dillon, Montserrado County
a4552.speech: Made a public apology regarding past criticisms, acknowledging the hypocrisy in leveraging allegations about private jet usage as a political weapon against President George Weah in 2023.

a4552.speaker: George Weah, former President of Liberia
a4552.speech: Openly confirmed his access to a private jet, insisting that the aircraft, valued at millions of dollars, was a gift from a friend in Burkina Faso.

a4567.speaker: Lisa Johnson, US Ambassador to Namibia
a4567.speech: Praised the new trade link with the United States, adding “The ‘Forest Stewardship Council’ has coined Namibian charcoal as ‘the greenest charcoal on the planet’, and the charcoal being sent to the United States is FSC-certified in terms of international standards for environmental, economic and social sustainability.”

a4567.speaker: Michael Degé, General Manager, Namibian Charcoal Association (NCA), speaking on behalf of exporters Africa Burns Charcoal and King Charcoal
a4567.speech: “the support of development partners, including USAID, has been key in advancing charcoal as a priority sector for export, and the event today represents many months of efforts to meet the necessary entry requirements because we appreciate that the US market is key to this export growth.”

a4571.speaker: World Bank Group (press release dated Washington, 28 February 2024)
a4571.speech: States that the overhaul is built around six changes relating to: a concentrated structure bringing together all guarantee experts, a simplified and comprehensive product offering, a streamlined process for reviews of guarantee instruments, greater accessibility of guarantees, a scaling-up, and new innovative tools; and that these rearrangements will eliminate redundant procedures in order to provide clients with transparency and certainty throughout the process, while offering new and innovative guarantee products allowing the private sector to engage further in resolving today's development challenges.

a4571.speaker: Ajay Banga, President of the World Bank
a4571.speech: "The resources and ingenuity of the private sector are indispensable to us in meeting the great global challenges" ; "By consolidating our offerings, simplifying processes and improving accessibility, we are giving businesses faster and easier access to guarantees."

a4571.speaker: Mark Carney, United Nations Special Envoy for Climate Action Finance and co-chair of the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ)
a4571.speech: Adds that the World Bank's new guarantee platform will make it possible to "provide guarantees on a larger scale and more quickly, and therefore more financing to help solve the world's most urgent problems."

a4571.speaker: G20 independent expert group (report on strengthening multilateral development banks)
a4571.speech: Called for increased use of guarantees to mitigate risk and catalyse private financing.

a4571.speaker: Shriti Vadera, chair of the British insurance company Prudential Plc
a4571.speech: Hopes that, by facilitating access to the full set of World Bank Group guarantees, the new guarantee platform will allow lenders and borrowers to better grasp the available options in order to plan investments with greater certainty.

a4571.speaker: Noel Quinn, Chief Executive Officer of HSBC Holdings Plc, member of the Private Sector Investment Lab
a4571.speech: "It will encourage reforms such as the harmonisation of contractual structures and will clarify the roles that public and private sector organisations must play to ensure the viability of projects."

a4587.speaker: Chinese Ambassador to Zambia (opinion article author)
a4587.speech: Wrote that "in the face of frequent occurrence of unilateralism, protectionism and economic bullying by a certain country for selfish gains, which has created severe difficulties for the world, China and African countries sent out a strong message for solidarity and cooperation of the Global South" ; Argued that "development assistance to African countries should be increased, not unilaterally slashed, to provide continued support to help African countries improve people's livelihood, reduce poverty and boost economic and social development," and that the international community should give prioritised attention to the economic difficulties and development challenges faced by African countries.

a4587.speaker: China-Africa Changsha Declaration on Upholding Solidarity and Cooperation of the Global South (document)
a4587.speech: Sent the message, in the firm belief that countries should uphold true multilateralism, safeguard the United Nations-centred international system, defend the World Trade Organisation-centred multilateral trading system and make economic globalisation more open, inclusive, mutually beneficial and balanced, so as to foster a better trade, investment and financing environment for the Global South.

a4587.speaker: China (announcement at the FOCAC ministerial coordinators' meeting)
a4587.speech: Announced that it will expand the zero-tariff treatment for 100 percent tariff lines to all 53 African countries having diplomatic relations with it, to help quality products from Africa access the Chinese market, and that for the least developed countries in Africa it will roll out further measures on market access, inspection and quarantine, and customs clearance.

a4587.speaker: Chinese Ambassador to Zambia (opinion article author)
a4587.speech: Said China and Zambia are all-weather friends and comprehensive strategic and cooperative partners, that "no matter how the international situation evolves, China's door to Zambia and Africa will only open wider," and expressed confidence that by advancing modernisation hand in hand, China and Zambia will further deepen the all-weather friendship and practical cooperation.

a4755.speaker: Isaias Angue Obama, FAO Resident Representative in Benin
a4755.speech: Notes that “the livestock sub-sector faces many challenges that must be met through a holistic approach to health, integrating human, animal and environmental health, and encouraging collaboration between the different sectors to prevent emerging and zoonotic diseases” ; explains that it is with this in mind that FAO joined forces with USAID in order, over the years, to improve the capacities of national veterinary services to respond to current and future animal health threats and to safeguard public health.

a4755.speaker: Isaias Angue Obama, FAO Resident Representative in Benin
a4755.speech: “This project lays the first stone for the creation of an ECTAD Centre for Benin. It is aligned with FAO’s strategic framework and with the various national planning instruments” ; recalls that the Emergency Centre for Animal Diseases is an FAO initiative aimed at helping countries detect, prevent and control transboundary animal diseases, a global network of emergency response and coordination working with national governments, regional organisations and other partners.

a4755.speaker: John Bernon, USAID representative in Benin
a4755.speech: “Our common objective is to support Benin in the crucial sectors of animal and environmental health. We are committed to strengthening national capacities for effective prevention, detection and response to the threats posed by emerging zoonotic infectious diseases, many of which originate in animals, and also antimicrobial resistance” ; indicates that the implementation of a multidisciplinary and multisectoral One Health approach at national and regional level is essential to effectively prevent and control these diseases transmitted between animals and humans.

a4755.speaker: Boubacar Mamadou Djaouga, representative of the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock and Fisheries
a4755.speech: “FAO is giving our country the opportunity to have veterinary services recognised as a global public good, strengthened as a good-governance tool through the FAO component of the Global Health Security (GHS) Africa project, which will be implemented by the Emergency Centre for Transboundary Animal Diseases (ECTAD).”

a4755.speaker: Sibylle Assavedo, representative of the Minister of Health
a4755.speech: “Health is a precious good, a common wealth that transcends borders. We are all bound by a shared responsibility towards our fellow citizens and towards humanity as a whole. It is this conviction that inspired the creation of GHS-Africa, an initiative aimed at strengthening global health security” ; “This project can only succeed through close collaboration between the actors. We must join forces, share our knowledge and our resources, and work together to strengthen global health security. Together we have the power to change the game.”

a4848.speaker: Harbi Bouh, head of Dire Dawa's Disaster Risk Management Coordination Office
a4848.speech: According to him, the Office has distributed materials worth 600,000 Birr, including clothes, sanitiser, and mattresses, and food items that cost about 700,000 Br to the victims.

a4848.speaker: Abdurrahman Birre, administrator of Kebele 09, Dire Dawa
a4848.speech: According to him, vulnerable households are being evacuated, people are taking shelter with their neighbours, and the city is collecting funds to buy housing materials for the victims, in a kebele where seven houses were completely destroyed and 60 houses partially ruined.

a4848.speaker: Udol Aguwa, head of the Gambela Regional State Government Press Secretariat
a4848.speech: According to him, over a million trees were destroyed by a flash flood in Godere Wereda after heavy rainfall that came down for two and a half consecutive hours on May 10, 2020.

a4848.speaker: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (UN-OCHA) report
a4848.speech: Seasonal flooding in April and May has so far affected 470,163 people, of whom some 301,284 people are displaced in Somali, Oromia, Afar, SNNP and Harari regional states as well as Dire Dawa City Administration ; "The situation is particularly severe in the Somali Regional State where more than 79pc of the flood-affected and displaced people are located," reads the report.

a4848.speaker: National Meteorology Agency (reports)
a4848.speech: The unprecedented heavy rainfalls during the last winter season, from December throughout February, is due to the ever-increasing warming of the northwestern Indian Ocean and positive Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) ; forecasts that unusually extensive rain is expected to fall in eastern, southeastern, southern, southwestern and central parts of the country in the coming weeks and months due to the northward progression of the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ).

a4848.speaker: Ahmedin Abdulkerim, communications affairs director at the National Meteorology Agency
a4848.speech: Said the heavy rainfalls were forecasted: "The Agency has been warning about the flash floods and the landslides" ; said concerned government offices should heed the forecasts the Agency projected and take precautionary measures such as evacuating potentially susceptible households and resettling them.

a4848.speaker: Debebe Zewde, public relations director at the National Disaster Risk Management Commission (NDRMC)
a4848.speech: According to him, the Commission has prepared food and non-food items and shelters to assist victims.

a4848.speaker: National Disaster Risk Management Commission (NDRMC)
a4848.speech: According to the Commission, in May 2020 around 21,000 people are likely to be affected by flash floods, and out of these 19,000 are anticipated to be vulnerable to displacement.

a4848.speaker: Malda Nadew, public relations head at UN-OCHA
a4848.speech: According to her, UN-OCHA Ethiopia has allocated 23 million dollars worth of non-food items provided by humanitarian assistance for prioritised IDPs.

a4848.speaker: Gemedo Dalle (PhD), associate professor of vegetation ecology and biodiversity management at Addis Abeba University and former Minister for Environment, Forest & Climate Change
a4848.speech: Said the severity of flash floods is aggravated by man-made factors such as soil degradation and deforestation: "The land is so degraded and eroded that it's unable to absorb and conserve the rainfall."

a4848.speaker: Gemedo Dalle (PhD), associate professor of vegetation ecology and biodiversity management at Addis Abeba University and former Minister for Environment, Forest & Climate Change
a4848.speech: Advised that working on early warning systems, evacuation and resettlement, and reforesting degraded areas with a non-cereal plant can be short-term solutions, and recommended land policy improvement as a long-term measure, including a clear-cut policy and strategy on land utilisation, institutionalised and consistent reforestation campaigns, integrative agricultural practices, settlement regulation and livelihood diversification, as well as an integrated approach from all government bodies ; "Rainfall is very important, and if we manage it improperly droughts will be caused which are even more disastrous than excess rainfall and floods," he added.

a4848.speaker: Tadesse Terefe, assistant professor of atmospheric physics and researcher at the Institute of Geophysics Space Science & Astronomy, Addis Abeba University
a4848.speech: Said the extensive rainfall is caused by the escalation of the positive Indian Ocean Dipole over the Horn of Africa, cold wind moisture pressure from northern Australia and hot moisture pressure from the coasts of Somalia ; said that because of the oscillation of the sea surface temperature between the southeastern and northwestern poles of the Indian Ocean, the southern and south-eastern parts of the country are more likely to experience the effects of the positive IOD and heavy rainfall ; "The hot and cold wind moisture from the northern and southern Indian Ocean couldn't traverse beyond East Africa because of cyclones in Madagascar, and the moisture pressure condenses there and results in heavy rainfall," said Tadesse. "Countries located in tropical East Africa are most likely to experience extensive and to some extent devastating rainfall because of the increasing occurrence of the positive Indian Ocean Dipole."

a4848.speaker: Tadesse Terefe, assistant professor of atmospheric physics and researcher at the Institute of Geophysics Space Science & Astronomy, Addis Abeba University
a4848.speech: Recommends that the government should heed meteorological predictions.

a4929.speaker: Federal Government of Nigeria
a4929.speech: Has said that local manufacturing of pharmaceuticals, vaccines, and medical devices is critical to achieving medicines security in Nigeria.

a4929.speaker: Olubunmi Aribeana, Director, Food and Drug Services, Ministry of Health and Social Welfare of Nigeria (represented by Adeola Olufowobi-Yusuf)
a4929.speech: Said that local manufacturing of pharmaceuticals also presents opportunities for job creation, international trade, economic growth and national security ; “We cannot afford to be caught flatfooted like during the Covid-19 pandemic” ; “All hands must be on deck to find innovative ways to achieving the goal of unlocking the health sector value chain. Nigeria needs to position itself in such a way as to maximally benefit from the African Free Trade Continental Area, which is adjudged to be among the largest in the world” ; said that local manufacturing would enhance sufficiency, affordable, accessible, good quality, and also reduce the nation's reliance on imported goods ; assured that the ministry would continue developing policies to attract investment and support the All-Government Initiative aimed at strengthening the pharmaceutical sector.

a4929.speaker: Omotayo Hamza, Supply Chain Management Officer of the World Health Organisation (WHO)
a4929.speech: Said Nigeria has sufficient policies and strategies in place, but often lacks implementation: “That is why, for this particular meeting, there is one key word that I love, and that is harmonisation. The Ministry of Trade is doing something about local production; the Ministry of Health is involved in something. Science and Technology too and these are the major stakeholders. We need to harmonise along that line for us to have a very strong agenda that is implementable, otherwise, we will have challenges.”

a4929.speaker: Chinelo Okonkwo, pharmacist
a4929.speech: Speaking on misgivings by some about the efficacy of Nigerian vaccines, said that they could be trusted as they go through all the stages of production before they could be certified fit for use; according to her, vaccine hesitancy is experienced all over the world and generally, there are adverse events following immunisation, but these are not enough to doubt the efficacy of Nigerian vaccines; assured that Nigerian pharmacies are well trained and able to deliver the best vaccines for Nigerians: “Our trust should be more on Nigerian products than the parallel imports. Vaccine itself is a cold chain molecule and in transporting them, if there is any break in that cold chain, that vaccine may not be potent. It is even better that it is produced here so that we can have it safe and efficacious for our people.”

a4929.speaker: Olajide Adebola, conference facilitator
a4929.speech: Said that the conference had the national and regional component and that the Presidential Initiative on Healthcare Value Chain (PVAC) had organised the conferences because it was important to have conversations on pharmaceutical issues; according to him, COVID-19 taught the nation a lot of lessons and the conferences would assess the present state of the sector and come up with viable solutions to achieving the PVAC: “We will examine how we have been able to fare under these new policies and government interventions, the executive orders? Is it reaching the grassroots, what advices and strategic recommendations at this point can we make to the government to update their current policy directions?”

a4929.speaker: Olajide Adebola, conference facilitator
a4929.speech: Speaking to the causes of high cost of medicines, said the cost of the import component of the medicines is the major factor driving up the costs, which would be addressed with the available government interventions in the sector: “Some years back, there are some medicines we could not manufacture, we imported them, but now we are manufacturing and that is the importance of having sound, evidence-based, defensible government policies. In near futures, cost of medicines will come down as all stakeholders and actors are acting towards ensuring safe medicines and affordable medicines for Nigeria.”

a4929.speaker: News Agency of Nigeria (NAN)
a4929.speech: Reports that the conference brought together relevant stakeholders to create a forum for engagement across public, private, and community sectors to contextualise PVAC; it would also identify actionable steps for enhancing local production of medicines and vaccines, and provide support in synthesising outcomes into policy and programme recommendations.

a5045.speaker: Available data (unattributed)
a5045.speech: According to available data, the cyclone directly affected the lives of 700,000 people, causing significant damage to housing, agricultural production and infrastructure, and claiming more than 60 lives.

a5129.speaker: Innocent Bashungwa, Tanzanian Minister for Works
a5129.speech: Told the 'Daily News' in an interview on the sidelines of the Tanzania-Japan Quality Infrastructure Dialogue that the determination of the government intends to smoothen urban mobility and speed up competitive economic development; said the Quality Infrastructure Dialogue highlights the Tanzanian government's unwavering commitment under President Samia Suluhu Hassan to leverage bilateral cooperation with Japan in advancing the transportation sector. “Efficient infrastructure is necessary for any country to compete in today's economy. Tanzania has already embarked on the journey of infrastructure transformation including designing the transport master plan, we are now looking on the financing side” ; “we are ready to fulfill the transformative journey.”

a5129.speaker: Innocent Bashungwa, Tanzanian Minister for Works
a5129.speech: Added that the focus is on the five major cities namely Dar es Salaam, Dodoma, Mbeya, Arusha and Mwanza, which are currently experiencing congestion; said Tanzania will develop a Quality Infrastructure Master Plan with Japan indicating construction projects, scope of work and resources needed, that it will be integrated in the 2025-2030 CCM election manifesto and will involve airports, railways, roads, bridges and flyovers to reduce time lost to congestion. “The country's major cities require new transport technologies to ensure that infrastructure such as roads, airports and railways complement one another” ; citing Dodoma, said the city is currently facing congestion after the launch of electric Standard Gauge Railway (SGR) train routes from Dar es Salaam to Dodoma.

a5129.speaker: Innocent Bashungwa, Tanzanian Minister for Works
a5129.speech: Told participants of the Quality Infrastructure Dialogue that Tanzania and Japan have a long-standing good relationship of 60 years and that both countries have been sharing experience and skills in various disciplines: “You have always been with us. Japan is a very dear partner to our country. It is the vision of our President to maintain this strong partnership between our two nations.”

a5129.speaker: Ogasawara Kenichi, Japan's Deputy Minister for International Projects
a5129.speech: Noted that this year's Quality Infrastructure Dialogue provides an opportunity for both countries to identify areas for strengthening partnerships and collaboration to enhance mutual economic development; said the dialogue also aims at promoting business and information exchanges between the two countries.

a5129.speaker: Misawa Yasushi, Japanese Ambassador to Tanzania
a5129.speech: Said the dialogue acts as the platform for fostering collaboration in human resource development between the two countries, which is the main ingredient of economic development; said in the next year (2025) Japan will host the World Expo which focuses on among others trade, in which Tanzania will also participate.

a5129.speaker: Baraka Luvanda, Tanzania's Ambassador to Japan
a5129.speech: Said Tanzania and Japan are only separated by ocean, echoing the stunning historic diplomatic relation between the two countries with this year's dialogue rooted on elevating the bilateral cooperation to a new height; said he was optimistic that the dialogue event will yield significant tangible outcomes to the two countries.

a5129.speaker: Gilead Teri, Executive Director of the Tanzania Investment Centre (TIC)
a5129.speech: Told the 'Daily News' that the Japanese Foreign Direct Investments (FDIs) between 1997 and 2024 stand at 42 million US dollar (114bn/-) for 24 projects in various sectors such as agriculture, manufacturing and commercial building; said the projects have created a total of 1,182 jobs and anticipated the infrastructure dialogue to further boost Japanese FDIs in Tanzania and Tanzanian exports to the Asian country.

a5506.speaker: Slovak opposition
a5506.speech: Justifies the motion with “the Government's steps, its statements, the barely transparent international visits led by the prime minister, Robert Fico, which call into question the country's international orientation.”

a5506.speaker: Slovak opposition
a5506.speech: Also criticises the recent criminal-law reform adopted by Fico's executive, which abolished the Special Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office and reduced the penalties for serious crimes, as well as the refounding of the public broadcaster RTVS, which is now under the control of the Ministry of Culture.

a5506.speaker: Robert Fico, Slovak Prime Minister
a5506.speech: Campaigned promising to withdraw support for Ukraine and, the day after his executive took office, announced the end of arms shipments to Kyiv, limiting Slovak support to “humanitarian and civilian aid.”

a5558.speaker: Nigeria Natural Medicine Development Agency (NNMDA)
a5558.speech: Has called for more training and documentation systems to advance evidence-based practice in traditional medicine.

a5558.speaker: Iziaq Salako, Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare
a5558.speech: Noted that the Strategic Plan of Action for Implementing the Traditional Medicine Policy and the Code of Ethics and Practice for Traditional Medicine Practitioners are designed to sanitise the sub-sector, boost safety and effectiveness, and prepare Nigeria for global competitiveness ; "This year's theme: Strengthen the Evidence Base for Traditional Medicine is both timely and critical as Africa seeks homegrown, context-specific solutions to its health challenges, particularly with dwindling overseas development assistance."

a5558.speaker: Iziaq Salako, Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare
a5558.speech: Stated that millions of Nigerians, particularly in rural communities, rely on traditional remedies as their primary healthcare option, making it a vital tool for improving access, generating employment, and supporting local manufacturing.

a5558.speaker: Iziaq Salako, Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare
a5558.speech: Highlighted achievements made so far by the government, including the creation of a Department of Traditional, Complementary and Alternative Medicine, the development of a Nigerian Herbal Pharmacopoeia, and the documentation of more than 200 plants on the Nigerian Essential Medicinal Plants List ; cited collaborations with the Standard Organisation of Nigeria (SON) to set quality standards, and the work of a ministerial committee on phytomedicine development and commercialisation ; added that Nigeria is also working with the West African Health Organisation and the World Health Organisation for technical support and knowledge exchange.

a5558.speaker: Iziaq Salako, Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare
a5558.speech: Acknowledged challenges, including the closure of the Federal College of Complementary and Alternative Medicine by the National Universities Commission in 2010, and said efforts are ongoing to revive the institution ; "The COVID-19 pandemic reminded the world of the importance of resilient and diversified healthcare systems and reignited interest in natural remedies. Nigeria and indeed the African continent must seize this momentum to bring traditional medicine to the global stage, with evidence as its passport."

a5558.speaker: Martins Emeje, Director General of NNMDA
a5558.speech: Said in his opening remarks at the NNMDA webinar in Lagos that research in the sector must be "culturally acceptable" and not ignored or hidden out of shame: "More than in any other area of health, people are even ashamed of talking about traditional medicine. But the truth is, it has been part of our lives for centuries. If we want to make progress, our research must be culturally acceptable."

a5558.speaker: John Tor-Agbidye, neurotoxicologist and integrative medicine expert (keynote speaker)
a5558.speech: Emphasised the need for proper record keeping and practitioner training; noted that about 70 per cent of Nigerians rely on traditional medicine, but most knowledge is passed orally by herbalists, bone setters, birth attendants, and healers, many of whom have little or no formal education ; "Documentation and training are the panacea for building credibility and trust in traditional medicine." ; "They foster integration into national health systems, encourage innovation and new drug discovery, and protect cultural heritage for future generations." ; recommended that the government strengthen laws and empower the Traditional Medicine Council, establish colleges and documentation centres, and promote collaborative research between NNMDA, universities, and other health institutions.

a5558.speaker: John Tor-Agbidye, neurotoxicologist and integrative medicine expert
a5558.speech: Said Nigeria could learn from countries such as China, India and Cuba, which have developed strong traditional medicine systems and trained Nigerian practitioners in recent years ; emphasised that through collaboration, the sector could attract funding from government, the private sector, and international organisations like the Bill Gates Foundation and Rockefeller Foundation ; added that Nigeria's biodiversity and growing global demand for natural products provide a major opportunity if remedies are validated and properly commercialised.

a5801.speaker: Executive Director of AFRYDEV, represented by Program Manager Edoka Ogwuche Abdullahi
a5801.speech: stated that the primary objective is to deepen understanding of the VAPP and Child Protection Laws, analyze state-level progress in their enforcement, and foster collaboration to address existing gaps while harmonizing implementation efforts across the BAY states.

a5887.speaker: James A.S. Momoh, Superintendent of the Monrovia Consolidated School System (MCSS)
a5887.speech: Has announced plans to establish a new Science, Technology, Engineering, and Math (STEM) school in Liberia to enhance the quality of education for MCSS students; speaking with our reporter over the weekend, revealed that MCSS is in discussions with Mrs. Marie Jilo Barnett, the Ambassador of Sierra Leone to Liberia, for the establishment of the school.

a5887.speaker: James A.S. Momoh, Superintendent of the Monrovia Consolidated School System (MCSS)
a5887.speech: Unveiled a series of transformative educational initiatives, including plans to enhance teacher training and expand vocational programs; revealed that MCSS has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Liberia Public School Project to supply essential school materials, and that agreements have been reached with USAID and AMEU to provide training for Early Childhood Development and elementary school teachers; "Two MCSS staff members were recently sent to South Korea to attend the International Youth Fellowship Education Conference" ; "This is part of our broader effort to expose our educators to international best practices in teaching."

a5887.speaker: James A.S. Momoh, Superintendent of the Monrovia Consolidated School System (MCSS)
a5887.speech: Mentioned ongoing discussions with local government officials, including Senator Craton Duncan and Representative P. Mark Juray, to secure support for MCSS' Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) programs; stated that a new training department has been established within MCSS to ensure teachers receive regular professional development; "We are also working towards establishing our own agricultural farm, and a department has already been set up for this purpose" ; "Furthermore, we are introducing agriculture and bookkeeping programs in our schools"; announced that MCSS is in discussions with GLOBAL ARCUS for scholarships aimed at teachers and confirmed that an MOU has been signed with the Sierra Leonean government to assist MCSS with capacity building; said these new initiatives demonstrate a strong commitment to improving educational standards within the MCSS.

a5887.speaker: Yekeh Kolubah, Representative
a5887.speech: Has pledged to assist in renovating and elevating the Rebecca J.N. Wilson Elementary School to a high school, utilizing funds from the district's development budget.

a5986.speaker: Russian government (statement)
a5986.speech: The government said on Thursday that Russia has temporarily banned exports of gasoline and diesel to all countries outside a circle of four ex-Soviet states with immediate effect in order to stabilise the domestic market, and that the ban did not apply to fuel supplied under inter-governmental agreements to members of the Moscow-led Eurasian Economic Union ; “Temporary restrictions will help saturate the fuel market, which in turn will reduce prices for consumers” ; “Previously, to stabilise the situation on the fuel market, the government raised the mandatory supply volumes of motor gasoline and diesel fuel to the commodity exchange. Daily monitoring of fuel purchases for the needs of agricultural producers with prompt adjustment of volumes has also been set up.”

a5986.speaker: Russian energy ministry
a5986.speech: Said the measure would prevent unauthorised “grey” exports of motor fuels.

a5986.speaker: Pavel Sorokin, Russian First Deputy Energy Minister
a5986.speech: Said the ban is indefinite and further actions will depend on the saturation of the market ; “We expect that the market will feel the effect quickly enough. But then it will depend on the saturation of the market and the results.”

a5986.speaker: Traders
a5986.speech: Say the fuel market has been hit by factors including maintenance at oil refineries, bottlenecks on railways and the weakness of the rouble, which incentivises fuel exports.

a5986.speaker: Traders and LSEG data
a5986.speech: Russia has already cut its seaborne diesel and gasoil exports by nearly 30 percent to about 1.7 million metric tons in the first 20 days of September compared to the same period in August, according to traders and LSEG data.

a6174.speaker: BBC report of 4 February 2025
a6174.speech: According to the report, France is suspected of exploiting NGOs to preserve its influence in Africa, with particular attention on Paris, which is deploying soft power strategies to respond to the increase in opposition to its customary diplomatic and military ties ; the report criticises the French government for continuing the struggle for its influence on the continent, saying that following the failure of the military presence, Paris is opting for a new approach by creating an innovative hybrid instrument to regain control of the former colonies, calling on human rights defenders, human rights protection groups and influential figures who will benefit from financial support and legal assistance from French embassies ; in the same document, the BBC states that certain French NGOs present on the continent are devoted not only to humanitarian aid but also to political manoeuvring, and Paris is criticised for exploiting its networks to promote French interests “under the pretext of defending human rights.”

a6174.speaker: Anonymous sources
a6174.speech: According to anonymous sources, Paris is planning to deploy these actions in ten African countries.

a6463.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli Prime Minister
a6463.speech: Vowed that Israel would continue pursuing Hamas leaders “wherever they are” ; speaking in Jerusalem alongside U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, said Israel was still assessing the outcome of the Doha strike.

a6463.speaker: Hamas
a6463.speech: Said five of its members were killed in the strike, though its leadership survived.

a6463.speaker: Draft summit resolution (seen by Reuters)
a6463.speech: The Doha summit is expected to issue a resolution warning that Israel’s “hostile acts,” including the strike on Qatar, endanger regional coexistence and undermine ongoing efforts to normalize ties with Israel ; an excerpt of the draft resolution accuses Israel of “genocide, ethnic cleansing, starvation, siege, colonization and expansionist policies,” warning that such actions threaten “everything achieved on the path of normalization with Israel.”

a6463.speaker: Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al-Thani, Qatari Emir
a6463.speech: Denounced the attack as “cowardly and treacherous,” revealing that Hamas leaders were reviewing a U.S.-backed ceasefire proposal mediated by Qatar and Egypt when the strike occurred.

a6463.speaker: Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman al-Thani, Qatar’s Prime Minister
a6463.speech: Added that Israeli aggression would not derail Doha’s mediation efforts alongside Washington and Cairo.

a6463.speaker: Marco Rubio, U.S. Secretary of State
a6463.speech: Urged Doha to continue playing a “constructive role” in resolving the conflict, particularly in securing the release of the 48 hostages still held in Gaza: “My message is that they have to be very, very careful. They have to do something about Hamas, but Qatar has been a great ally to the United States” ; voiced firm U.S. support for Israel, signaling Washington’s continued alignment with Netanyahu’s government.

a6463.speaker: World’s largest association of genocide scholars
a6463.speech: Israel has faced mounting accusations of genocide in Gaza, including from the world’s largest association of genocide scholars.

a6463.speaker: Local authorities in Gaza
a6463.speech: Say the campaign has killed more than 64,000 Palestinians.

a6463.speaker: Israel (government position) / Israeli figures
a6463.speech: Israel rejects the charge of genocide, citing its right to self-defense after the October 7 attacks, which killed 1,200 people and resulted in 251 hostages, according to Israeli figures.

a6463.speaker: Local health officials (Gaza City)
a6463.speech: Reported at least 16 Palestinians killed in strikes on two homes and a tent sheltering displaced families.

a6463.speaker: Israeli military (the army)
a6463.speech: Claimed the high-rise 16-floor building it demolished in Gaza concealed “terrorist infrastructure,” after warning residents to evacuate.

a6535.speaker: Alice Ruhweza, President of the Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa (AGRA)
a6535.speech: “The future of African agriculture will not be bankrolled by donors. It will be driven by investors.” ; “There’s still money out there. What’s missing is a compelling investment case.” ; “We’ve spent two decades testing models that work. We know that if yields hit three metric tons per hectare, the business case is strong. Now we must speak the language of investors: ROI, scale, and resilience.”

a6535.speaker: Alice Ruhweza, President of the Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa (AGRA)
a6535.speech: Said, referencing the Maputo and Malabo Declarations, “For 20 years, we’ve been urging governments to meet the 10% public investment pledge in agriculture. But the money just isn’t there. Many are drowning in debt, spending nearly half of their GDP on repayments.”

a6535.speaker: Alice Ruhweza, President of the Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa (AGRA)
a6535.speech: “This isn’t just about maize. It’s about processing. It’s about trade. It’s about industries that create value, not just calories.”

a6535.speaker: Alice Ruhweza, President of the Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa (AGRA)
a6535.speech: Urged governments to strengthen the capacity of banks, financial institutions, and agri-entrepreneurs to attract and deploy private capital: “We must move from subsidies to sustainability. From donor dependency to deal-making.”

a6535.speaker: Alice Ruhweza, President of the Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa (AGRA)
a6535.speech: Pointed to Mastercard’s recent multi-million-dollar investment in African agriculture—not as aid, but as business: “They’re not here for charity. They see jobs, growth, and market potential. That’s the shift we need.”

a6535.speaker: Alice Ruhweza, President of the Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa (AGRA)
a6535.speech: “You can have the best seed and science, but if the farmer doesn’t see a buyer, she won’t plant. That’s why we must build strong, reliable market systems—and that’s where private capital must come in.” ; “We can’t design 21st-century food systems if we’re still excluding the people doing the actual work.”

a6535.speaker: Alice Ruhweza, President of the Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa (AGRA)
a6535.speech: Offered Malawi’s leaders both a challenge and a roadmap: “Stop waiting for aid. Start unlocking investment. Build policies that support agribusiness—from rural banks and export incentives to infrastructure.”

a6535.speaker: Alice Ruhweza, President of the Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa (AGRA)
a6535.speech: “We’re country-led. We’re impact-led. And we’re people-focused.” ; “Africa is the youngest continent on Earth. Agriculture is its largest employer. The opportunity is staggering—if we’re bold enough to seize it.”

a6801.speaker: Gilbert Houngbo, Director-General of the International Labour Organisation (ILO)
a6801.speech: Called for stronger international cooperation to address pressing global labour challenges and advance social justice worldwide; in statements delivered at the World Bank Group/IMF Annual Meetings in Washington D.C. underlined the need for coordinated action to tackle unemployment, inequality and the impacts of climate change on the world of work ; “The complex challenges facing the global labour market require a united and collaborative approach. International cooperation is not just beneficial; it is essential for creating a more equitable and sustainable future of work.”

a6801.speaker: Gilbert Houngbo, Director-General of the International Labour Organisation (ILO)
a6801.speech: Pointed out the Global Coalition for Social Justice, an ILO initiative launched in November 2023, as a key platform for collective action and advocacy for global social justice ; “With over 300 partners, including more than 85 governments and 40 international organisations, the coalition is driving concrete actions to reduce inequalities, alleviate poverty and advance social justice globally.”

a6801.speaker: International Labour Organisation (ILO)
a6801.speech: According to ILO, the coalition's ability to bring together a diverse range of stakeholders into a cohesive and transformative partnership is especially significant, “given the systemic inequalities and complex economic challenges facing the world today”; the United Nations agency's latest projections indicate that, while the global unemployment rate is expected to be 4.9 percent in 2024 and 2025, the distribution of job gaps is uneven, with women and developing countries in particular facing significant challenges.

a6801.speaker: Gilbert Houngbo, Director-General of the International Labour Organisation (ILO)
a6801.speech: “While we see some positive trends in certain economies, labour underutilisation remains pervasive globally. We must focus our collective efforts on creating quality jobs and extending social protection to all workers, particularly in developing countries.” ; addressed the “critical need” for increased financing and investment in social protection, education, healthcare and employment policies.

a6801.speaker: Gilbert Houngbo, Director-General of the International Labour Organisation (ILO)
a6801.speech: Called for a renewed commitment to international development cooperation, emphasising its role in supporting countries under financial stress ; “Official Development Assistance remains crucial, especially for African countries facing significant financing gaps in ensuring universal social protection. We urge developed countries to fulfil their commitments and scale up their assistance.”

a6801.speaker: Various stakeholders / activists (Malawi)
a6801.speech: Have been advocating for coordinated action to create quality jobs and boost local employment, with a strong emphasis on empowering women in the workforce and reducing gender disparities and improving access to financial support for vulnerable populations; activists in the field of quality education are calling for increased investment in the sector to enhance human capital.

a6909.speaker: Emmanuella Zamba, Permanent Secretary of the Lagos State Health Management Agency (LASHMA)
a6909.speech: Speaking at the event, listed the agency’s achievements to include the rollout of an equity fund that guarantees healthcare access for over 300,000 vulnerable residents ; “Today, 12 December, is globally recognised as UHC Day. In Lagos State, we are committed to ensuring that everyone has access to quality healthcare through Ilera Eko, our state health insurance scheme” ; Said the equity fund, supported by 1 per cent of Lagos state’s consolidated revenue, sets a benchmark, ensuring funds are consistently available for vulnerable groups ; Noted that LASHMA will intensify its public awareness campaign to encourage Lagosians to subscribe to Ilera Eko before enforcement begins next year ; “Health insurance is a safety net. It guarantees that you and your family can access care without financial hardship. This is our message during this walk and beyond.”

a6909.speaker: Emmanuella Zamba, Permanent Secretary of LASHMA
a6909.speech: Praised Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu’s leadership, describing him as Lagos State’s UHC Brand Ambassador ; “His executive order making health insurance mandatory underscores his dedication to universal health. We are working to ensure that every Lagosian can access affordable, quality healthcare, irrespective of their financial situation.”

a6909.speaker: Statement issued after the event
a6909.speech: According to a statement issued after the event, the walk attracted stakeholders across various sectors, reinforcing the government’s commitment to health equity.

a6909.speaker: Lagos State Health Management Agency (LASHMA)
a6909.speech: Recently revealed that over 1.3 million residents have been enrolled in the Ilera-Eko insurance scheme, noting that since the enactment of the Lagos State Health Scheme Law in 2015, the state has significantly advanced toward its UHC goals.

a6909.speaker: Bodunrin Osikomaiya, Executive Secretary of the Lagos State Blood Transfusion Service
a6909.speech: Highlighted the integration of blood transfusion services into Ilera Eko: “Residents, including those with sickle cell disorder, can access blood units under the plan, ensuring equity in healthcare delivery. The government’s commitment to making healthcare accessible is truly commendable.”

a6909.speaker: Chidumga Ohazurike, Senior Health Specialist at USAID’s Local Health System Sustainability Project
a6909.speech: Lauded Lagos State’s progress in UHC implementation: “We have witnessed the state’s commitment to equity funds and policy enactments. USAID remains a proud partner in this transformative journey.”

a6909.speaker: Biodun Omoloja, Head of the Global Fund Grant Management Unit
a6909.speech: “Through partnerships and funding, we aim to place over 23,000 vulnerable individuals on health insurance, ensuring no one is left behind.”

a7139.speaker: ActionAid Nigeria
a7139.speech: According to ActionAid, the graduates of the HDP Nexus Academy, selected from across various sectors, took training designed to build capacity for addressing the complex challenges posed by crises and conflicts around Nigeria.

a7139.speaker: Mr Andrew Mamedu, Country Director of ActionAid (represented at the ceremony by David Habba)
a7139.speech: Said efforts through the HDP Nexus and the academy in particular reflect ActionAid's commitment to nurturing innovative approaches to humanitarian responses, sustainable development, and peace efforts ; said Nigeria stands at a critical time when the HDP Nexus is most important: "We need a new way of working," he stressed, adding that the graduates from the HDP Nexus Practitioners Academy had been equiped with insights to integrate HDP Nexus principles in their respective spheres of influence ; said it was to address the challenges of disjointed responses that ActionAid Nigeria partnered with UniMaid, AUN, and NSUK and established the HDP Practitioners Academy Campus to provide training and capacity building for HDP practitioners and communities.

a7225.speaker: Edmond Moukala Ngouemo, UNESCO Representative to Ghana
a7225.speech: Said Ghana had faced the destructive impacts of extreme weather, including severe floods and droughts, and that the events of 2023, including the Akosombo Dam spillage that displaced tens of thousands and the drought that affected over one million people across eight regions, had highlighted the urgency of their collective action.

a7225.speaker: Edmond Moukala Ngouemo, UNESCO Representative to Ghana
a7225.speech: Pointed out that the exciting thing about the project was its potential to empower communities, explaining that through gender-inclusive and youth-centred approaches, they aimed to cultivate local leadership and ownership ; said by equipping people with knowledge and tools, they were planting seeds for a sustainable future in which communities became the champions of climate resilience.

a7225.speaker: Yoshimoto Hiroshi, Japan's Ambassador to Ghana
a7225.speech: Said Japan had been at the forefront of disaster risk reduction and climate change mitigation, and that that commitment was reflected in its continuous support for global initiatives, including the Sendai Framework of Disaster Risk Reduction, which aligned directly with the project's goal, particularly in enhancing early warning systems and strengthening institutional and community resilience ; said Japan, which was prone to natural disasters, including flooding and earthquake-tsunami, had successfully implemented early warning systems and infrastructure improvements to mitigate these risks ; said that guided by its official development assistance principle of "Leave no one behind," which aligned with the Sustainable Development Goal (SDG), Japan was actively working to ensure that developing countries such as Ghana received the necessary support to strengthen their resilience against climate-related disasters.

a7225.speaker: Dr Bernadette Araba Adjei, Director of Legal Affairs of the Water Resources Commission (Ghana)
a7225.speech: Expressed the commission's gratitude to the government of Japan for funding the project, which she said would ultimately help Ghana achieve the goals set out in SDG Six on water and sanitation for the population of Ghana.
